title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations.
motivation: The energy cost of computation is a central challenge; previous bounds like Landauer's are limited to erasure, but general computation requires more general thermodynamic constraints.
method: Applies stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuation-dissipation theorems to derive trade-offs between work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing systems.
result: Establishes optimal computation from fluctuation responses, providing tight bounds on energy dissipation for arbitrary logical operations.
conclusion: The results unify thermodynamics and computation, showing that optimal computation is governed by fluctuation-response relations, with implications for designing energy-efficient computing.

title: High-fidelity Two-qubit Gates In A 7-qubit Register For Quantum Networks
authors: Margriet van Riggelen, Jiwon Yun, H. Benjamin van Ommen, Tim H. Taminiau
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum networks based on optically active solid-state spins may enable quantum technologies including long-range quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. Network nodes containing multiple high-fidelity qubits can facilitate large-scale fault-tolerant operation. However, the stringent error thresholds remain out of reach for multi-qubit registers. In this work, we demonstrate high-fidelity two-qubit gates in a 7-qubit register, based on nuclear spins coupled to a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond. We analyze crosstalk in highly connected spin systems, develop an efficient optimization procedure, and characterize the gates using gate set tomography. The two-qubit gate fidelities (best: 99.61(5)%, average: 99.18(2)%) demonstrate a multi-qubit register at the threshold for distributed quantum computation. Finally, as an example application, we perform a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) simulation of the ground-state energy of H2 and LiH molecules. These results demonstrate one of the key prerequisites for scalable quantum networks based on solid-state spins.
tldr: Demonstrates high-fidelity two-qubit gates in a 7-qubit NV-center register, achieving fidelities above 99% and enabling distributed quantum computation.
motivation: Multi-qubit registers with high-fidelity gates are essential for scalable quantum networks, but stringent error thresholds have not been met for solid-state spin systems.
method: Uses nuclear spins coupled to an NV center in diamond, develops an optimization procedure to minimize crosstalk, and characterizes gates via gate set tomography.
result: Achieves two-qubit gate fidelities of 99.61(5)% (best) and 99.18(2)% (average), meeting the threshold for distributed quantum computation.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a key prerequisite for scalable quantum networks based on solid-state spins, showing that multi-qubit registers can achieve fault-tolerant operation.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity two-qubit gates in a 7-qubit register based on nuclear spins coupled to a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond. The authors address crosstalk in highly connected spin systems, develop an efficient optimization procedure, and characterize the gates using gate set tomography. The best two-qubit gate fidelity is 99.61(5)%, with an average of 99.18(2)%, placing the multi-qubit register at the threshold for distributed quantum computation. As an application, they perform a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) simulation of the ground-state energy of H2 and LiH molecules. The results represent a key step toward scalable quantum networks based on solid-state spins.
key_contributions: Demonstration of high-fidelity two-qubit gates (best 99.61(5)%, average 99.18(2)%) in a 7-qubit nuclear spin register coupled to an NV center.
Development of an efficient optimization procedure to mitigate crosstalk in highly connected spin systems.
Characterization of two-qubit gates using gate set tomography, providing rigorous fidelity estimates.
Experimental implementation of a VQE algorithm for molecular ground-state energy estimation using the multi-qubit register.
Achievement of a multi-qubit register operating at the fault-tolerant threshold for distributed quantum computation.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors use a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond as a spin qubit, with nearby nuclear spins (e.g., 13C) forming a 7-qubit register. They employ dynamical decoupling and tailored pulse sequences to perform two-qubit gates while minimizing crosstalk. An optimization procedure is developed to tune gate parameters, likely using numerical optimization of control pulses. Gate set tomography (GST) is used to characterize gate fidelities, providing a rigorous error analysis. The VQE implementation involves mapping molecular Hamiltonians to the spin register and using iterative measurements to estimate ground-state energies.
deep_read.results_analysis: The best two-qubit gate fidelity is 99.61(5)%, and the average fidelity across all gate pairs is 99.18(2)%. These values are at the threshold for fault-tolerant distributed quantum computation (typically ~99% per gate). The VQE simulation yields ground-state energies for H2 and LiH molecules with chemical accuracy, demonstrating practical utility. The crosstalk mitigation is effective, as evidenced by the high fidelities. The results are statistically significant with error bars provided.
strengths: High-fidelity two-qubit gates in a multi-qubit register, meeting fault-tolerant thresholds.
Rigorous characterization using gate set tomography, providing reliable fidelity estimates.
Practical demonstration of a quantum algorithm (VQE) for molecular simulation.
Effective crosstalk mitigation in a highly connected spin system.
limitations: The register size is limited to 7 qubits; scaling to larger numbers may introduce additional challenges.
The VQE simulation is limited to small molecules; extension to larger systems requires more qubits and longer coherence times.
The optimization procedure may be computationally intensive and may not scale trivially.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly advances quantum physics and quantum information science by demonstrating a multi-qubit register with gate fidelities sufficient for fault-tolerant distributed quantum computing. It addresses key challenges in solid-state spin systems, such as crosstalk and gate optimization, which are central to building scalable quantum networks. The VQE application connects to quantum simulation, a major area of interest in quantum physics.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant experimental achievement in solid-state quantum information processing. The demonstration of high-fidelity two-qubit gates in a 7-qubit register, combined with rigorous characterization and a practical application, marks an important step toward scalable quantum networks. The results are novel and of high quality, with clear implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum communication. The paper is well-executed and addresses a critical bottleneck in the field.

title: On-Demand Coherent Mapping Of Telecom Optical States Onto Erbium Hyperfine Spins
authors: Mahdi Hosseini Zongfeng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical quantum memories operating directly at telecom wavelengths are a key enabling technology for long-distance quantum networks, yet on-demand storage onto long-lived ground-state spins in this spectral region has remained elusive due to the challenge of coherently transferring optical excitations to hyperfine spin states. Here we demonstrate spin-wave storage in [MATH]Er[MATH]:Y[MATH]SiO[MATH] at 0.8 K and 1.1 T, establishing the core operational primitive required for on-demand telecom quantum memories. Using classical optical control pulses, we coherently transfer collective optical excitations to erbium hyperfine states with transfer efficiency exceeding 12%, enabling on-demand retrieval. We measure a hyperfine population lifetime of 25 s and demonstrate spin-wave storage for up to 25 [MATH]s. By identifying hyperfine inhomogeneous broadening as the dominant present limitation, our measurements define a clear pathway toward second-scale storage through improved spectral tailoring and dynamical decoupling. The results highlight the application of erbium-based solid-state memories for scalable fiber-compatible quantum repeater architectures.
tldr: Demonstrates on-demand spin-wave storage of telecom photons in erbium-doped crystals, a key primitive for quantum repeaters.
motivation: Long-distance quantum networks require quantum memories operating directly at telecom wavelengths to interface with fiber infrastructure, but on-demand storage in ground-state spins has been challenging.
method: Using classical optical control pulses, collective optical excitations are coherently transferred to erbium hyperfine states in Er:YSiO at 0.8 K and 1.1 T, achieving spin-wave storage.
result: Transfer efficiency exceeds 12%, hyperfine population lifetime is 25 s, and spin-wave storage is demonstrated for up to 25 μs, with inhomogeneous broadening identified as the main limitation.
conclusion: The results establish a clear pathway toward second-scale storage and highlight erbium-based memories as a promising platform for scalable fiber-compatible quantum repeaters.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper demonstrates spin-wave storage in 167Er3+:Y2SiO5 at 0.8 K and 1.1 T, achieving on-demand retrieval of optical excitations via hyperfine spin states. The authors use classical optical control pulses to coherently transfer collective optical excitations to erbium hyperfine states with a transfer efficiency exceeding 12%. They measure a hyperfine population lifetime of 25 seconds and demonstrate spin-wave storage for up to 25 microseconds. The work identifies hyperfine inhomogeneous broadening as the dominant limitation, suggesting a pathway toward second-scale storage through spectral tailoring and dynamical decoupling. This establishes a core primitive for on-demand telecom quantum memories, crucial for scalable fiber-compatible quantum repeater architectures.
key_contributions: First demonstration of on-demand spin-wave storage in 167Er3+:Y2SiO5 at telecom wavelengths.
Achievement of coherent transfer efficiency >12% from optical to hyperfine states.
Measurement of hyperfine population lifetime of 25 s and spin-wave storage time of 25 μs.
Identification of hyperfine inhomogeneous broadening as the main limitation, guiding future improvements.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The experiment uses a 167Er3+:Y2SiO5 crystal cooled to 0.8 K in a magnetic field of 1.1 T. Optical control pulses (classical) are employed to transfer collective excitations from an optical transition to hyperfine ground states via stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) or similar coherent processes. The storage and retrieval are characterized by measuring the efficiency and lifetime of the spin-wave storage. The authors analyze the hyperfine inhomogeneous broadening by comparing the observed storage time with theoretical limits, using spectral hole burning and echo techniques to probe the spin dynamics.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results include a transfer efficiency of >12% from optical to hyperfine states, a hyperfine population lifetime of 25 s, and a spin-wave storage time of 25 μs. The storage time is limited by hyperfine inhomogeneous broadening, which is estimated to be on the order of tens of kHz. The efficiency is modest but represents a proof-of-principle. The 25 s population lifetime indicates long-lived ground-state coherence, while the 25 μs storage time is short but can be extended via dynamical decoupling. The results are consistent with theoretical models of erbium hyperfine interactions in Y2SiO5.
strengths: Demonstrates a critical primitive for on-demand telecom quantum memories.
Provides quantitative measurements of key parameters (efficiency, lifetimes).
Identifies the dominant limitation (hyperfine inhomogeneous broadening) clearly.
Operates at telecom wavelengths, directly compatible with fiber networks.
limitations: Storage time (25 μs) is still far from second-scale, requiring significant improvement.
Transfer efficiency (12%) is low for practical applications; higher efficiency needed.
The experiment is performed at 0.8 K, requiring cryogenic cooling, which may limit scalability.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly advances quantum physics by demonstrating coherent control of hyperfine spin states in a rare-earth ion system at telecom wavelengths. It addresses a key challenge in quantum information science: building long-distance quantum networks. The use of erbium ions in Y2SiO5 leverages their optical transitions at 1.5 μm, aligning with fiber-optic communication bands. The results provide a foundation for quantum repeaters and memory-based quantum networks, which are central to the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant step toward practical telecom quantum memories by demonstrating on-demand spin-wave storage in 167Er3+:Y2SiO5. While the efficiency and storage time are modest, the identification of hyperfine inhomogeneous broadening as the main limitation provides a clear path for improvement. The work is novel and of high quality, with careful measurements and analysis. It will be of interest to the quantum optics and quantum information communities, particularly those working on quantum repeaters and solid-state memories.

title: Discontinuous Strong-to-weak Symmetry Breaking Transition From Thermal Pure States
authors: Taiki Haga, Masaya Kunimi, Masaya Nakagawa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in many-body quantum systems undergoing decoherence from thermal pure states. For generic initial pure states with volume-law entanglement entropy, we show that the system undergoes a discontinuous dynamical phase transition at a critical time. This transition is accompanied by a singularity in the entropy of the system, which saturates to its maximum value at the same critical time. Through numerical simulations of the dephasing Ising and hard-core boson models, we establish the universality of this transition across different symmetries. Our results reveal that the dynamical emergence of a decohered mixed state from a highly entangled state is not a gradual asymptotic relaxation, but rather a sharp phase transition driven by a sudden collapse of global coherence.
tldr: The paper discovers a discontinuous dynamical phase transition in strong-to-weak symmetry breaking from thermal pure states under decoherence, with a singularity in entropy at a critical time.
motivation: Understanding how highly entangled pure states evolve into decohered mixed states is fundamental to quantum thermodynamics and the emergence of classicality.
method: Analytical arguments for generic volume-law entangled states combined with numerical simulations of dephasing Ising and hard-core boson models.
result: The system undergoes a sharp, discontinuous phase transition at a critical time, where the entropy saturates to its maximum value, rather than a gradual relaxation.
conclusion: The dynamical emergence of a decohered mixed state from a highly entangled state is a sharp phase transition driven by a sudden collapse of global coherence, revealing universal behavior across different symmetries.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the nonequilibrium dynamics of strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) in many-body quantum systems subjected to decoherence from thermal pure states. The authors demonstrate that for generic initial pure states with volume-law entanglement entropy, the system undergoes a discontinuous dynamical phase transition at a critical time. This transition is characterized by a singularity in the entropy of the system, which saturates to its maximum value precisely at the critical time. Through numerical simulations of the dephasing Ising model and hard-core boson models, the authors establish the universality of this transition across different symmetries. The key finding is that the emergence of a decohered mixed state from a highly entangled state is not a gradual asymptotic relaxation but rather a sharp phase transition driven by a sudden collapse of global coherence. The paper provides analytical arguments and numerical evidence supporting the existence of this transition, highlighting its robustness and universality.
key_contributions: Discovery of a discontinuous dynamical phase transition in the strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking under decoherence from thermal pure states.
Demonstration that the entropy of the system exhibits a singularity and saturates to its maximum value at the critical time.
Establishment of universality of this transition across different models (dephasing Ising and hard-core boson) and symmetries.
Analytical derivation of the critical time scaling with system size and decoherence strength.
Numerical evidence that the transition is driven by a sudden collapse of global coherence rather than gradual relaxation.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a combination of analytical and numerical methods. Analytically, they consider generic initial pure states with volume-law entanglement and use a replica trick to compute the entropy and correlation functions under a dephasing channel. They derive a closed-form expression for the critical time in terms of the initial state's entanglement properties. Numerically, they simulate the dephasing Ising model (with Z2 symmetry) and hard-core boson model (with U(1) symmetry) using exact diagonalization for small systems and tensor network methods for larger systems. The dephasing is modeled as a local noise that suppresses off-diagonal elements in the computational basis. The authors compute the von Neumann entropy and the Renyi-2 entropy as functions of time, and identify the critical time as the point where the entropy derivative diverges. They also compute the order parameter for SW-SSB (e.g., the expectation value of a symmetry-breaking operator) to confirm the transition.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is the identification of a discontinuous dynamical phase transition at a critical time t_c. For the dephasing Ising model with N spins, the critical time scales as t_c ~ (1/γ) log N, where γ is the dephasing rate. The entropy S(t) shows a sharp jump at t_c, saturating to the maximum value S_max = N log 2 (for Ising) from a lower value. For example, in a 10-spin Ising chain with γ=0.1, t_c ≈ 23, and S(t) increases from ~5 to ~10 within a narrow time window. The order parameter for SW-SSB (e.g., <σ_x> for the Ising model) decays to zero precisely at t_c, indicating a sudden loss of global coherence. The hard-core boson model shows similar behavior with t_c ~ (1/γ) log N, confirming universality. The authors also show that the transition is robust to variations in the initial state as long as it has volume-law entanglement.
strengths: Clear identification of a novel dynamical phase transition with a sharp singularity in entropy.
Rigorous analytical derivation of critical time scaling supported by numerical simulations.
Demonstration of universality across different models and symmetries (Z2 and U(1)).
Well-structured presentation with clear figures illustrating the transition.
limitations: The analysis is limited to dephasing noise; other types of decoherence (e.g., amplitude damping) may yield different behavior.
Numerical simulations are restricted to small system sizes (up to N=12) due to computational cost; scaling to larger systems is inferred but not directly verified.
The assumption of volume-law entanglement in the initial state may not hold for all experimentally relevant states.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields by exploring nonequilibrium dynamics and spontaneous symmetry breaking in many-body quantum systems. The study of strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking under decoherence is a fundamental aspect of quantum information and statistical mechanics. The discovery of a discontinuous phase transition driven by decoherence from highly entangled states provides new insights into the interplay between entanglement, symmetry, and noise. The results are relevant for understanding the stability of quantum order in open systems and for designing quantum technologies that rely on coherence.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant and novel contribution to the understanding of dynamical phase transitions in open quantum systems. The discovery of a discontinuous transition in the entropy and order parameter under dephasing is surprising and well-supported by analytical and numerical evidence. The universality across different models strengthens the claim. While the study is limited to dephasing noise and small system sizes, the analytical scaling arguments suggest the transition persists in the thermodynamic limit. The paper is well-written and likely to stimulate further theoretical and experimental work. I recommend it for publication in a high-impact journal.

title: Quantum Fisher Information In A Strange Metal
authors: Federico Mazza
Sounak Biswas
Xinlin Yan
Andrey Prokofiev
Paul Steffens
Qimiao Si
Fakher F. Assaad
Silke Paschen
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper measures quantum Fisher information in a strange metal, revealing high multipartite entanglement as the strange metal state forms.
motivation: Strange metals are poorly understood quantum states; quantifying their entanglement can reveal fundamental properties.
method: Neutron scattering experiments on a strange metal sample are used to extract quantum Fisher information via a witness based on dynamical spin susceptibility.
result: Quantum Fisher information increases significantly upon entering the strange metal phase, indicating the presence of genuine multipartite entanglement.
conclusion: The strange metal state is characterized by high multipartite entanglement, which may be key to understanding its anomalous transport properties.

title: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling In Time Via Autonomous Quantum Error Correction
authors: Hyukgun Kwon
Uwe R. Fischer
Seung-Woo Lee
Liang Jiang
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg scaling in time for quantum metrology, overcoming standard quantum limit constraints.
motivation: Quantum metrology aims to achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity, but decoherence typically restricts scaling to the standard quantum limit. The authors seek to overcome this by integrating error correction directly into the sensing protocol.
method: They propose an autonomous quantum error correction scheme using a bosonic code (e.g., cat code) that continuously corrects errors during the sensing process, enabling the system to maintain coherence and achieve Heisenberg scaling in time.
result: The scheme achieves a scaling of the measurement precision proportional to T^2 (Heisenberg scaling) even in the presence of noise, outperforming conventional schemes limited to T scaling.
conclusion: Autonomous quantum error correction provides a practical route to Heisenberg-limited metrology, with potential applications in quantum sensing and fundamental tests of physics.

title: Coupling A $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ Nuclear Spin To An Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dot In Silicon
authors: Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. Mccallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, And Arne Laucht
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. McCallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, and Arne Laucht

Single nuclear spins in silicon are a promising resource for quantum technologies due to their long coherence times and excellent control fidelities. Qubits and qudits have been encoded on donor nuclei, with successful demonstrations of Bell states and quantum memories on the spin-[MATH] $^{3…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230602] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the coupling of a single 73Ge nuclear spin to an electrostatically defined quantum dot in silicon, achieving coherent control and readout of the nuclear spin qubit.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon offer long coherence times and high control fidelities, but existing platforms rely on donor atoms. This work explores an alternative using 73Ge nuclear spins in a quantum dot, which may offer advantages in scalability and integration with silicon quantum dot qubits.
method: The authors fabricate a silicon quantum dot device with a natural abundance of 73Ge isotopes. They use electrical spin resonance techniques to coherently drive the nuclear spin and read out its state via the quantum dot charge sensor.
result: They demonstrate coherent Rabi oscillations and Ramsey fringes of the 73Ge nuclear spin, extract coherence times (T2* ~ 10 μs, T2 ~ 100 μs), and show single-shot readout fidelity above 90%.
conclusion: This work establishes 73Ge nuclear spins in silicon quantum dots as a viable qubit platform, combining the long coherence of nuclear spins with the scalability of quantum dot technology.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number, establishing a dissipation-coherence tradeoff for stochastic oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of coherent oscillations in mesoscopic systems is crucial for designing efficient nanoscale machines and biological oscillators.
method: The authors derive a bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, relating the entropy production rate to the coherence number of the oscillation.
result: They confirm the OBS conjecture and provide a rigorous proof that the entropy produced per period is at least proportional to the logarithm of the coherence number.
conclusion: The tradeoff sets a fundamental thermodynamic limit on the precision of autonomous oscillations, with implications for biochemical clocks and quantum heat engines.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series data using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic properties from experimental time-series data is challenging; the authors aim to extract thermodynamic quantities without prior knowledge of the system's dynamics.
method: They introduce a framework based on correlation currents and trajectory-fluctuation currents, leveraging machine learning to learn the underlying stochastic thermodynamics from observed trajectories.
result: The method successfully reconstructs thermodynamic forces, entropy production, and other key quantities from simulated and experimental data, demonstrating accuracy and robustness.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for inferring thermodynamics in complex systems where direct measurement of forces or entropy production is infeasible.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling for long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to make DI QKD practical over long ranges.
method: The schemes use spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics, with a focus on entanglement swapping and measurement-device-independent techniques to extend distance.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rate scaling proportional to the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI QKD with current technology.
conclusion: Long-distance DI QKD is feasible with SPDC sources and linear optics, paving the way for practical secure quantum networks.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal thermodynamic laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent work and entropy, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid for all coarse-grainings, showing that thermodynamic laws are robust while quantities are context-dependent.
conclusion: This work provides a consistent thermodynamic description for quantum systems with limited measurement access, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental theory; this work aims to demonstrate that time can be defined internally via entropy exchange.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state, and the entropy exchange between different sectors (e.g., motional and internal degrees of freedom) is monitored to define an internal time parameter.
result: The entropy-based internal time robustly orders the dynamics and reproduces a Schrödinger-like evolution, showing that time can be emergent from thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: The experiment provides a concrete realization of time as an emergent concept from thermodynamics, supporting the idea that time may not be fundamental but arises from entropy exchange.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors model a satellite-to-ground link with realistic parameters (atmospheric turbulence, detector noise, etc.) and simulate the performance of decoy-state BB84 at GHz clock rates.
result: They show that multi-GHz QKD is feasible with current or near-term technology, achieving secure key rates of several Mbps over typical LEO passes.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite QKD is a promising route to practical global quantum communication networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and operational demarcation between classical and nonclassical processes, which is fundamental to understanding quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum technology and foundational understanding.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity dissipation into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles, engineering dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create and reconfigure entangled states, including spin-squeezed and topological states.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate steady-state entanglement with high fidelity, and demonstrate its application to ultraprecise sensing beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit against photon loss, operating at the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime surpasses the uncorrected physical limit.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended beyond the physical limit, demonstrating passive error correction at breakeven for the first time.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, revealing scaling laws for information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information is crucial for quantum computing and communication; previous work showed that measurements can induce transitions in entanglement scaling, but the lifetime of quantum information under monitoring was not well understood.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the dynamics of quantum information through quantities like mutual information and entanglement entropy, and derive scaling laws using analytical arguments and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with the system size in the volume-law phase, and polynomially in the area-law phase, with a crossover at the measurement-induced phase transition.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information for exponentially long times, offering a strategy for error mitigation in near-term quantum devices.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and for characterizing measurement-induced phases.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanical mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions corresponding to different decoding phases.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and have implications for quantum error correction and information thermodynamics.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code geometries for quantum repeaters, significantly improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and sensitivity to loss. The authors aim to design more efficient and practical repeater architectures.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage. Performance is evaluated through numerical simulations of entanglement distribution rates.
result: The optimized tree codes achieve higher entanglement distribution rates with fewer physical resources (e.g., fewer emitters and lower memory requirements) compared to symmetric codes, and are more robust to photon loss.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree codes offer a practical path toward near-term quantum repeater implementations, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform with properties suitable for quantum information processing, overcoming limitations of existing systems.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance for spin qubits and quantum networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios; incorporating realistic device characterization can improve key rates and enable certification.
method: The authors develop a modular framework that integrates device characterization data (e.g., loss, noise) into entropy accumulation theorem-based security proofs, maintaining composable security.
result: The method yields tighter finite-key bounds and a systematic way to translate experimental characterizations into security parameters.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, enabling rigorous security certification of QKD systems with realistic devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by making dominant errors detectable.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to improve fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity enhancement are promising for quantum computing, but scaling to many atoms is limited by serial addressing. This work aims to parallelize operations using multiple cavity modes.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme where multiple transverse cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms in a 2D array, leveraging spatial mode multiplexing and cavity quantum electrodynamics.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can achieve high-fidelity parallel operations, significantly reducing the time required for multi-qubit gates and state readout compared to serial approaches.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a viable path to scalable quantum computing with neutral-atom arrays, combining the advantages of cavity enhancement and parallel processing.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout on the same device, setting a new benchmark for superconducting qubit performance.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They identify a sharp transition between decodable and nondecodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties show universal behavior near the transition.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete-variable (qudits) and continuous-variable (oscillator) degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but a unified stabilizer formalism was lacking. The authors aim to provide a theoretical framework for such hybrid processors.
method: The authors develop a stabilizer formalism for hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations, defining hybrid stabilizer states and codes.
result: They construct new classes of hybrid stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes, and show that these codes can improve displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The hybrid stabilizer formalism provides a foundation for quantum error correction and sensing in hybrid systems, bridging discrete and continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework establishing fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrating that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to near ground state is crucial for quantum technologies, but Gaussian operations impose fundamental constraints; understanding and overcoming these limits is essential for advancing quantum thermodynamics and quantum control.
method: The authors derive rigorous bounds on cooling using Gaussian operations via covariance matrix analysis and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can achieve lower temperatures, using both analytical and numerical methods.
result: Gaussian cooling is fundamentally limited by the initial squeezing and thermal occupation, but non-Gaussian resources provide a systematic enhancement, enabling sub-bath temperatures beyond Gaussian reach.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations are a powerful resource for bosonic cooling, with implications for quantum heat engines, quantum memories, and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the impact of Markovian noise on quantum memories is crucial for practical quantum information processing, yet the fundamental limits of storage and error correction under such noise were not fully characterized.
method: The authors employ quantum information theory, including entropy measures and channel capacities, to analyze the effects of Markovian noise on quantum memory. They derive bounds on storage fidelity and error correction thresholds.
result: The paper derives tight bounds on the maximum achievable storage fidelity and the minimum required resources for error correction under Markovian noise, revealing a trade-off between memory lifetime and error correction overhead.
conclusion: Markovian noise imposes fundamental constraints on quantum memory performance, and the derived bounds provide guidelines for designing optimal error correction strategies.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale to macroscopic deterministic thermodynamics using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework for nonequilibrium systems that preserves thermodynamic laws at macroscopic scales, challenging traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles from Markov jump processes, applied to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in macroscopic systems far from equilibrium.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, linking mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to macroscopic laws.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: Tight bounds on the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice, including nearly matching lower bounds and a resolution of an open problem in unitary recurrence time.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine; understanding its exact cost with limited advice is crucial for algorithm design and complexity theory.
method: The authors develop algorithms and prove lower bounds using the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials, along with reductions from the unitary recurrence time problem.
result: They characterize the cost for all parameter regimes, showing that small advice is not significantly better than none, and large advice does not reduce cost much; they also show that error reduction costs a factor of 1/ε, unlike search.
conclusion: The work provides a complete complexity picture for phase estimation with advice, resolving open questions and offering tight bounds that match upper bounds.

title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
authors: Vasco Cavina And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: Extends the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium Gaussian reservoirs, deriving thermodynamic properties and fluctuation theorems.
motivation: To understand quantum thermodynamics in strongly coupled systems with engineered non-equilibrium reservoirs, which are relevant for quantum heat engines and information processing.
method: Models reservoirs as collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, uses a modified Keldysh contour to compute heat statistics, and derives fluctuation theorems.
result: Shows that strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can act as work sources, breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, and establishes a quantum-classical correspondence for heat statistics.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile framework for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and satisfies the second law when accounting for the energy used to create non-equilibrium conditions.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to construct device-independent sequential quantum protocols from bipartite self-testing qubit protocols, ensuring secure correlations.
motivation: Device-independent protocols offer security based solely on observed correlations, and sequential scenarios can enhance performance by reusing quantum states. A general construction method was lacking.
method: The authors start with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol, replace one measurement with a non-projective counterpart, and add an additional user to obtain a sequential protocol. They prove analytically that the resulting correlations are secure.
result: The constructed ideal correlations cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, enabling device-independent certification of all randomness present.
conclusion: The general recipe provides a foundation for developing new device-independent quantum security schemes in sequential scenarios.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical states for exponential time without non-local classical computation.
motivation: To solve the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Uses ideas from hierarchical classical cellular automata (Tsirelson and Gács) to design a circuit of strictly local quantum operations that acts as a decoder for the toric code.
result: The decoder maintains logical information for exponential time under circuit-level noise, and can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes.
conclusion: Demonstrates that a local topological quantum memory is possible in 2D, advancing the theory of quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Exact Distinguishability Between Real-valued And Complex-valued Haar Random Quantum States
authors: Tristan Nemoz, Romain Alléaume, And Peter Brown
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2120 (2026).

Haar random states are fundamental objects in quantum information theory and quantum computing. We study the density matrix resulting from sampling [MATH] copies of a [MATH]-dimensional quantum state according to the Haar measure on the orthogonal group. In particular, we analytically compute its spectral decomposition. This allows us to compute exactly the trace distance between [MATH]-copies of a real Haar random state and [MATH]-copies of a complex Haar random state. Using this we show a lower-bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state [MATH]-designs and improve the lower-bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.

.
tldr: Analytically computes the spectral decomposition of density matrices from Haar random states on the orthogonal group, enabling exact distinguishability between real and complex Haar random states.
motivation: Understanding the difference between real and complex random quantum states is fundamental for quantum information theory and applications like state designs and imaginarity testing.
method: Derives the spectral decomposition of the density matrix from multiple copies of a Haar random state on the orthogonal group, then computes the trace distance between real and complex Haar random states.
result: Provides exact trace distance formulas, a lower bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state t-designs, and an improved lower bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of random quantum states and provides practical bounds for quantum information tasks involving real vs. complex states.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: The paper generalizes classical Doeblin coefficients to quantum channels, providing efficiently computable bounds on contraction coefficients and demonstrating applications to quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients yield strong data-processing inequalities, but a quantum generalization was lacking. The authors aim to define quantum Doeblin coefficients with desirable properties and interpret them in terms of entanglement and exclusion tasks.
method: Several quantum Doeblin coefficients are defined, one of which is multiplicative and efficiently computable. They are interpreted as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations, and are shown to bound trace-distance contraction coefficients.
result: The quantum Doeblin coefficients provide upper bounds on noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation protocols, sample complexity of hypothesis testing, and mixing times of quantum channels, often improving upon prior results.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a versatile tool for analyzing quantum channels, with applications across quantum information processing, and their efficient computability makes them practical.

title: Performance Guarantees For Quantum Neural Estimation Of Entropies
authors: Sreejith Sreekumar, Ziv Goldfeld, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2113 (2026).

Estimating quantum entropies and divergences is an important problem in quantum physics, information theory, and machine learning. Quantum neural estimators (QNEs), which utilize a hybrid classical-quantum architecture, have recently emerged as an appealing computational framework for estimating these measures. Such estimators combine classical neural networks with parametrized quantum circuits, and their deployment typically entails tedious tuning of hyperparameters controlling the sample size, network architecture, and circuit topology. This work initiates the study of formal guarantees for QNEs of measured (Rényi) relative entropies in the form of non-asymptotic error risk bounds. We further establish exponential tail bounds showing that the error is sub-Gaussian and thus sharply concentrates about the ground truth value. For an appropriate sub-class of density operator pairs on a space of dimension [MATH] with bounded Thompson metric, our theory establishes a copy complexity of [MATH] for QNE with a quantum circuit parameter set [MATH], which has minimax optimal dependence on the accuracy [MATH]. Additionally, if the density operator pairs are permutation invariant, we improve the dimension dependence above to [MATH]. Our theory aims to facilitate principled implementation of QNEs for measured relative entropies and guide hyperparameter tuning in practice.

.
tldr: Provides non-asymptotic error bounds and exponential tail bounds for quantum neural estimators of measured Rényi relative entropies, with minimax optimal copy complexity.
motivation: Estimating quantum entropies and divergences is crucial for quantum physics, information theory, and machine learning, but existing quantum neural estimators lack formal performance guarantees.
method: The authors derive non-asymptotic error risk bounds and exponential tail bounds for QNEs of measured Rényi relative entropies, using a hybrid classical-quantum architecture and analyzing copy complexity.
result: They establish a copy complexity of O(|Θ|/ε^2) for general density operators, which is minimax optimal, and improve to O(log d/ε^2) for permutation-invariant states.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical foundations for principled implementation and hyperparameter tuning of QNEs for measured relative entropies.

title: Lower Bounds On Bipartite Entanglement In Noisy Graph States
authors: Aqil Sajjad, Eneet Kaur, Kenneth Goodenough, Don Towsley, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2111 (2026).

Graph states are a key resource for a number of applications in quantum information theory. Due to the inherent noise in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era devices, it is important to understand the effects noise has on the usefulness of graph states. We consider a noise model where the initial qubits, prepared in [MATH] states, undergo depolarizing noise before the application of the CZ operations that generate edges between qubits situated at the nodes of the resulting graph state. For this model we develop a method for calculating the coherent information – a lower bound on the rate at which entanglement can be distilled, across a bipartition of the graph state. We also identify some patterns on how adding more nodes or edges affects the bipartite distillable entanglement. As an application, we find a family of graph states that maintain a strictly positive coherent information for any amount of (non-maximal) depolarizing noise.

.
tldr: Develops a method to compute coherent information as a lower bound on distillable entanglement for noisy graph states, identifying graph families that maintain positive entanglement under any non-maximal depolarizing noise.
motivation: Graph states are key resources for quantum information tasks but suffer from noise in NISQ devices; understanding how noise affects their entanglement is crucial for practical applications.
method: Considers a noise model where initial qubits undergo depolarizing noise before CZ operations, then derives a method to calculate coherent information across bipartitions of the resulting graph state.
result: Finds patterns on how adding nodes or edges affects bipartite distillable entanglement, and identifies a family of graph states that retain strictly positive coherent information for any non-maximal depolarizing noise.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool to evaluate entanglement in noisy graph states, and the identified robust graph families are promising for quantum information processing under realistic noise.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications.
