title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable dynamics and the connection to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep links to quantum circuit models.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has irrational index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that preserve a symmetry subalgebra, which is relevant to topological phases and dualities.
method: Uses algebraic classification with two invariants: anyon permutation symmetry and a generalized GNVW index, and constructs generating operations.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs for finite Abelian group symmetries, and demonstrates that the Kramers-Wannier duality corresponds to a nontrivial anyon permutation with irrational index.
conclusion: Subalgebra QCAs are classified by anyon permutations and an index, and cannot always be extended to full QCAs, revealing nontrivial mixing with translations.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement using spin-squeezed states in lossy multi-path atom interferometers, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but losses degrade performance. The authors aim to quantify achievable gains under realistic conditions.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses from velocity selectivity and scattering. One-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated for phase sensitivity.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing degree can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses, but finite temperature reduces benefits.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic losses, but practical challenges like temperature must be addressed to realize gains.

title: Symmetry-induced Logarithmic Relaxation In The Quantum Kicked Rotor
authors: Julien Hébraud, Floriane Arrouas, Bruno Peaudecerf, Juliette Billy, David Guéry-Odelin, Olivier Giraud, Bertrand Georgeot, Gabriel Lemarié And Christian Miniatura
abstract: We study the effect of discrete symmetries on coherent multiple scattering in the quantum kicked rotor. When the initial momentum is set to zero—as in recent Bose–Einstein condensate experiments—the effective pseudo-disorder becomes even under momentum inversion. The resulting discrete mirror symmetry of the dynamics profoundly alters spectral correlations: it generates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets localised at opposite momenta, whose exponentially small splittings produce a hierarchy of exponentially large dynamical timescales. The coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks then exhibit a striking non-monotonic evolution and strongly asymmetric contrasts, followed by an exceptionally slow logarithmic relaxation toward a common asymptotic value—a hallmark of glassy dynamics, here emerging in a fully coherent quantum system. That such archetypal glass-like behaviour arises from a single discrete symmetry constraint reveals an unexpected and deep connection between quantum coherence and slow relaxation phenomena.
tldr: This paper shows that discrete mirror symmetry in the quantum kicked rotor leads to glassy logarithmic relaxation, linking symmetry to slow dynamics.
motivation: To understand how discrete symmetries affect coherent multiple scattering and spectral correlations in a paradigmatic quantum chaotic system.
method: Analytical and numerical study of the quantum kicked rotor with zero initial momentum, analyzing Floquet quasienergies and coherent backscattering/forward-scattering peaks.
result: Mirror symmetry creates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets with exponentially small splittings, causing non-monotonic evolution and logarithmic relaxation of scattering peaks.
conclusion: A single discrete symmetry can produce glassy dynamics in a fully coherent quantum system, revealing a deep connection between symmetry and slow relaxation.

title: Optimizing Qubo On A Quantum Computer By Mimicking Imaginary Time Evolution
authors: Yahui Chai And Alice Di Tucci
abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum–classical algorithm for solving quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems using an imaginary time evolution-mimicking circuit (ITEMC). The circuit parameters are optimized to mimic short-time ITE, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values. This significantly reduces the measurement overhead by avoiding full energy evaluation. By updating the initial state based on results from last step iteratively, the algorithm quickly converges to the low-energy solutions. With a pre-sorting step that optimizes quantum gate ordering based on QUBO coefficients, the convergence is further improved. Our classical simulations achieve approximation ratios above up to 150 qubits. Furthermore, the linear scaling of entanglement entropy with system size suggests that the circuit is challenging to simulate classically using tensor networks. We also demonstrate hardware runs on IBM’s device for 40, 60, and 80 qubits, and obtain solutions compatible with that from simulated annealing.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for solving QUBO problems using a circuit that mimics imaginary time evolution.
motivation: QUBO problems are important for combinatorial optimization, but current quantum algorithms require many measurements or deep circuits; this work aims to reduce measurement overhead and improve convergence.
method: The algorithm optimizes circuit parameters to mimic short-time imaginary time evolution using only single- and two-qubit expectation values, avoiding full energy evaluation. It iteratively updates the initial state and includes a pre-sorting step for gate ordering.
result: Classical simulations achieve high approximation ratios for up to 150 qubits, and hardware runs on IBM devices for 40, 60, and 80 qubits yield solutions comparable to simulated annealing.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical approach to QUBO on near-term quantum devices, with linear scaling of entanglement entropy indicating classical hardness.

title: Hybrid Monte Carlo For Fractional Quantum Hall States
authors: Ting-Tung Wang, Ha Quang Trung, Qianhui Xu, Min Long, Bo Yang And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: We develop a hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) method to efficiently compute the physical observables from the samplings of the Laughlin and the Moore–Read (MR) wave functions of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems. With the advancements in methodology, including global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry, our HMC simulation is significantly faster than the widely used Metropolis Monte Carlo scheme. As a result, we can readily simulate systems with electron numbers on both disk and sphere geometries. We apply this method to investigate the topological shift obtained from the edge dipole moment, computed from the wave function density on the disk. We also numerically computed the non-Abelian braiding matrices for different braiding schemes of the MR quasiholes on the sphere. Results with much better quality compared with previous works have been achieved. With the thermodynamic limit results obtained at ease, we also discuss the future usage of our method to clarify the questions on the instability of FQH states in an ideal Chern band setting or under quantum decoherence.
tldr: Develops a hybrid Monte Carlo method for simulating fractional quantum Hall wave functions, focusing on computational efficiency and topological properties.
motivation: Efficiently compute observables from Laughlin and Moore-Read wave functions for large systems, overcoming limitations of standard Metropolis Monte Carlo.
method: Uses hybrid Monte Carlo with global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry to sample FQH wave functions.
result: Achieves significantly faster simulations, enabling computation of topological shift and non-Abelian braiding matrices with improved quality.
conclusion: The method facilitates thermodynamic limit studies and can address questions about FQH state stability in Chern bands or under decoherence.

title: Upconversion Dual-comb Passive Spectroscopy Of Mid-IR Incoherent Light
authors: Mingchen Liu, Matthew Heyrich, Sichong Ma, Scott A. Diddams
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce cross-comb correlation spectroscopy, which correlates signals from asynchronous sum-frequency sampling of mid-IR incoherent light with two near-IR combs. We experimentally measure the frequency of phase-randomized mid-IR light with 100-MHz resolution using near-IR detectors.
tldr: This paper presents a novel spectroscopic technique using dual-comb correlation to measure mid-IR incoherent light with near-IR detectors.
motivation: Mid-IR spectroscopy is important for chemical sensing but typically requires specialized detectors; the authors aim to leverage near-IR detectors for mid-IR measurements.
method: They use two near-IR frequency combs to perform asynchronous sum-frequency sampling of mid-IR incoherent light, correlating the signals to extract spectral information.
result: They experimentally demonstrate 100-MHz resolution frequency measurement of phase-randomized mid-IR light using near-IR detectors.
conclusion: Cross-comb correlation spectroscopy enables high-resolution mid-IR spectroscopy with standard near-IR detectors, potentially simplifying experimental setups.

title: Finite-Element Matrix Product States For Continuum Models In One Dimension
authors: Akshay Shankar, Karel van Acoleyen, Jutho Haegeman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a matrix product state framework for simulating one-dimensional quantum many-body systems in the continuum using non-orthogonal single-particle basis sets. By mapping the physical problem to an auxiliary computational space, we show that the resulting many-body overlap operator can be efficiently encoded as a matrix product operator for sufficiently localized orbitals, thereby generalizing a construction that first appeared in [arXiv:2405.10285]. This construction recasts the variational ground-state search into a generalized eigenvalue problem, which can be solved using a generalized density matrix renormalization group algorithm. As a primary application, we employ a first-order finite-element expansion to study the ground state properties of the Lieb-Liniger gas in the presence of inhomogeneities. This approach also provides a natural setting for exactly refining the lattice, thereby enabling multigrid optimization strategies for matrix product states.
tldr: This paper develops a matrix product state framework for continuum quantum many-body systems using finite-element basis sets, enabling efficient ground-state simulations of the Lieb-Liniger gas.
motivation: Simulating quantum many-body systems in the continuum is challenging due to the need for large basis sets; the authors aim to leverage matrix product states for efficient variational calculations.
method: They map the physical problem to an auxiliary computational space using non-orthogonal single-particle basis functions, encode the many-body overlap operator as a matrix product operator, and solve a generalized eigenvalue problem with a generalized DMRG algorithm.
result: The method is applied to the Lieb-Liniger gas with inhomogeneities, demonstrating accurate ground-state properties and enabling multigrid optimization strategies.
conclusion: The finite-element matrix product state approach provides a natural and efficient way to simulate one-dimensional continuum models, with potential for further algorithmic improvements.

title: Quantum Simulation Of The Liouville Equation In Classical Mechanics With Discontinuous Potential Via Schr\"odingerization
authors: Shuyi Zhang Shi Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop quantum simulation algorithms for the Liouville equation of classical mechanics with discontinuous potential. Such discontinuities represent potential barriers at which classical particles undergo energy preserving transmission or reflection, and the resulting interface conditions must be incorporated into the numerical flux. We combine Hamiltonian-preserving schemes by Jin and Wen in Commun. Math. Sci. 3(3), 285-315 (2005) with the Schr\"odingerization method, which embeds the resulting nonunitary semi-discrete dynamics into a unitary Schr\"odinger type system in one additional auxiliary variable [arXiv:2212.14703, arXiv:2212.13969]. For one-, two-, and [MATH]-dimensional problems with grid aligned interfaces, we construct sparse matrix representations of the transmission and reflection fluxes using step and hat functions, derive the corresponding Hamiltonians of the Schr\"odingerized systems, and analyze their sparse-access query complexity. In the sparse-access oracle model, the resulting algorithms have a polynomial dependence on the inverse accuracy and avoid the exponential dependence on the phase-space dimension suffered by classical grid based Hamiltonian-preserving schemes, up to the cost of implementing the oracles and the postselection overhead. We also describe the postselected recovery of the physical solution state and the quantum readout of macroscopic observables such as density and averaged velocity through overlap estimation. Numerical experiments based on classical simulation of the Schr\"odingerized dynamics validate the proposed formulation and illustrate the correct transmission/reflection behavior at potential barriers.
tldr: This paper develops quantum simulation algorithms for the Liouville equation with discontinuous potentials using Schrödingerization, focusing on classical mechanics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Classical simulation of the Liouville equation with discontinuous potentials suffers from exponential scaling in phase-space dimension. The authors aim to leverage quantum algorithms to overcome this bottleneck.
method: They combine Hamiltonian-preserving numerical schemes with the Schrödingerization method, which embeds nonunitary dynamics into a unitary Schrödinger-type system via an auxiliary variable. Sparse matrix representations of transmission/reflection fluxes are constructed.
result: The quantum algorithms achieve polynomial dependence on inverse accuracy and avoid exponential scaling in phase-space dimension, up to oracle and postselection costs. Numerical experiments validate correct transmission/reflection behavior.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a quantum advantage for simulating classical mechanics with discontinuous potentials, but the work is primarily a quantum algorithm for classical dynamics, not directly aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Regrid-qaoa: A Resource-Efficient Graph-Reduced Hybrid Qaoa Framework For Physics-Constrained Power System Islanding
authors: Yuqi Jiang, Yuqi Zhang, Zhiding Liang, Qiang Guan, Yan Li, Ganesh Kumar Venayagamoorthy
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing has rapidly emerged as a powerful paradigm for tackling computationally demanding problems. In particular, quantum optimization shows strong promise for hard combinatorial problems in power systems, where increasing distributed energy penetration heightens the need for intentional islanding to maintain grid reliability and resilience. However, power system islanding is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem that becomes computationally prohibitive for classical solvers as network size grows, motivating the use of quantum computing as a promising alternative pipeline. This study develops a resource-efficient hybrid QAOA islanding framework that brings physics-constrained power-system partitioning into the quantum optimization workflow. The framework combines coherency-informed graph reduction, physics-aware constraint modeling, and structured post-processing to efficiently convert shallow-circuit QAOA samples into high-quality feasible islanding decisions without deep circuits or large shot budgets. The proposed framework is validated on the standard IEEE benchmark systems (9-, 14-, 24-, 30-, 39-, and 57-bus), demonstrating that the hybrid workflow achieves Gurobi-optimal solution quality with a clear quantum resource advantage over vanilla QAOA, while the resulting islanding solutions satisfy all physical feasibility requirements after network separation. This study establishes QAOA-based islanding as a viable quantum approach for critical infrastructure, with structured post-processing as the key enabler of quantum resource efficiency.
tldr: This paper proposes a resource-efficient hybrid QAOA framework for power system islanding, combining graph reduction and physics-aware constraints.
motivation: Power system islanding is an NP-hard combinatorial problem that becomes computationally prohibitive for classical solvers as network size grows, motivating the use of quantum computing.
method: The framework integrates coherency-informed graph reduction, physics-aware constraint modeling, and structured post-processing to convert shallow-circuit QAOA samples into feasible islanding decisions.
result: Validated on IEEE benchmark systems (9- to 57-bus), the hybrid workflow achieves Gurobi-optimal solution quality with a clear quantum resource advantage over vanilla QAOA.
conclusion: QAOA-based islanding is a viable quantum approach for critical infrastructure, with structured post-processing enabling quantum resource efficiency.

title: Single Nanoparticle Dynamics In Opto-Thermal Tweezers: Resolving The Temporal Resolution Of Depletion Force Trapping
authors: Jinchao Chen, Robert Talla Kontchou, Saurabh Rai, Guillaume Baffou, Sylvain Blaize, Quanbo Jiang, J\'er\^ome Wenger
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optothermal tweezers enable the manipulation of a wide range of nano-objects through optically induced depletion forces. Despite significant advances, the temporal dynamics of optothermal trapping remain elusive, as existing methodologies rely almost exclusively on time and ensemble averaging. Consequently, stable trapping cannot be distinguished from local transient accumulation, where the time-averaged concentration increases but particles exhibit rapid, dynamic motion in and out of the trap. Here we investigate optothermal trapping with single-nanoparticle-level analysis and sub-millisecond temporal resolution. Our data resolve the elusive dynamics of 40 nm polystyrene nanoparticles trapped within depletion force potentials in polyethylene glycol solutions, enabling to differentiate the conditions leading to extended trapping times from those leading to transient localization. Numerical simulations corroborate our experimental findings, elucidating how the interplay between thermophoresis and diffusiophoresis governs nanoparticle dynamics. These insights deepen our mechanistic understanding of optothermal trapping and unlock opportunities for single-molecule studies, nanoscale assembly, and targeted drug delivery.
tldr: This paper studies the temporal dynamics of optothermal trapping of nanoparticles using single-particle tracking and sub-millisecond resolution.
motivation: Existing methods rely on time averaging, which cannot distinguish stable trapping from transient accumulation. Understanding the dynamics is crucial for applications in single-molecule studies and nanoscale assembly.
method: Experimental setup with optothermal tweezers and 40 nm polystyrene nanoparticles in PEG solutions, combined with numerical simulations of thermophoresis and diffusiophoresis.
result: The data resolve trapping dynamics at single-nanoparticle level, differentiating extended trapping from transient localization, and simulations elucidate the interplay of thermophoresis and diffusiophoresis.
conclusion: The insights deepen mechanistic understanding of optothermal trapping and enable applications in single-molecule studies, nanoscale assembly, and drug delivery.

title: Quantum-classical Hybrid Models Based On Error Correction For Time Series Forecasting
authors: Jonathan H. A. de Carvalho, Filipe C. de L. Duarte, Fernando M. de Paula Neto, Paulo S. G. de Mattos Neto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time series forecasting largely benefits from combining the strengths of different models, especially using a scheme where a model corrects another model by capturing supplementary patterns from forecasting errors. Concurrently, quantum models are providing a means to augment the classical capacity, including in time series forecasting, by acting alongside classical models in hybrid architectures. In this work, we propose the first forecasting system based on error correction that jointly uses quantum and classical models. Here, quantum models first extract patterns by exploring quantum phenomena, and classical models capture the remaining patterns from the quantum errors. Compared to classical single models and classical-classical hybrid models based on error correction, the complementary capacity that emerges from this quantum-classical system provided the best results in most of the addressed problems. Therefore, this work paves the way to introduce quantum models in established hybridization schemes for time series forecasting.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum-classical model for time series forecasting using error correction, where quantum models extract patterns and classical models correct errors.
motivation: Time series forecasting benefits from combining models, and quantum models may enhance classical capacity. The paper aims to introduce quantum models into established error-correction hybridization schemes.
method: A quantum-classical hybrid system where quantum models first extract patterns, then classical models capture remaining patterns from quantum errors, using an error correction framework.
result: The hybrid quantum-classical model outperformed classical single models and classical-classical hybrids in most tested time series forecasting problems.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of quantum-classical hybrid models based on error correction for time series forecasting, paving the way for further integration of quantum models in hybridization schemes.

title: Inverted Dirac Oscillator
authors: Mustapha Maamache
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Dirac oscillator is obtained from the Dirac Hamiltonian [MATH] by modifying the momentum through a non-Hermitian substitution [MATH]. Despite the non-Hermitian nature of this momentum operator, the full Hamiltonian remains Hermitian due to the presence of the Dirac matrix [MATH]. However, if one instead introduces a Hermitian modification of the form [MATH], the resulting Hamiltonian is no longer Hermitian. In this case, the system corresponds to an inverted Dirac oscillator [MATH], where the potential becomes unbounded from below, the energy spectrum becomes continuous, and the eigenfunctions fail to be square-integrable, leading to normalization difficulties. We show that the Hamiltonian [MATH] is a pseudo-[MATH]-symmetric operator, and we introduce an unbounded, non-unitary transformation that establishes a connection between [MATH] and [MATH]. The purpose of this work is to analyze this relativistic quantum system -- known as the Dirac inverted oscillator -- which, despite its various applications, admits an exact analytical solution.
tldr: The paper studies an inverted Dirac oscillator with a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, showing it is pseudo-Hermitian and connecting it to the standard Dirac oscillator via an unbounded transformation.
motivation: To analyze the inverted Dirac oscillator, which has applications but admits an exact analytical solution despite its unbounded potential and continuous spectrum.
method: The authors introduce a non-Hermitian modification to the Dirac Hamiltonian, identify pseudo-Hermiticity, and construct an unbounded non-unitary transformation linking the inverted and standard oscillators.
result: The inverted Dirac oscillator Hamiltonian is pseudo-Hermitian, its energy spectrum is continuous, and eigenfunctions are not square-integrable; the transformation maps it to the standard Dirac oscillator.
conclusion: The inverted Dirac oscillator is exactly solvable and related to the standard Dirac oscillator via a non-unitary transformation, but its physical interpretation remains challenging due to non-Hermiticity.

title: Multi-channel High-speed Flip-chip Packaging Platform For Thin-film Lithium Niobate Photonic Circuits
authors: Zhenzheng Wang, Xiangzhi Xie, Yikun Chen, Yifan Wu, Zeyu Luo, Hanke Feng, Yulong Chen, Zengyi Xu, Zixi Wang, Yuansong Zeng, Mandie Huang, Ke Zhang, Yingxia Liu, Cheng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To address the urgent need for multi-channel high-speed electrical interfacing of thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) photonic circuits, we realize a flip-chip packaging platform capable of simultaneously delivering 13 high-speed and 32 low-speed electronic signals to a centimeter-sized TFLN chip. The platform exhibits low flip-chip bonding loss and low inter-channel crosstalk over a broad bandwidth up to 50 GHz. Leveraging this packaging platform, we demonstrate high-speed electrical interfacing with two proof-of-concept TFLN photonic circuits, namely a 2x8 optical switch and an electro-optic comb-based transmitter. The switch achieves arbitrary 8-channel routing with ~3 dB insertion loss, < -20 dB crosstalk, and an equipment-limited switching time of <= 34 ps. The transmitter circuit includes a 50 GHz electro-optic comb generator with 2.8-dB flatness, a tunable microring to arbitrarily filter one comb line, and a modulator for data transmission at 20 Gbit/s. The packaging platform could significantly advance large-scale TFLN circuits in optical communications, microwave photonics, and photonic computing.
tldr: A flip-chip packaging platform for thin-film lithium niobate photonic circuits enabling multi-channel high-speed electrical interfacing.
motivation: To address the need for high-speed electrical interfacing of TFLN photonic circuits for applications in optical communications and computing.
method: Fabrication of a flip-chip packaging platform with 13 high-speed and 32 low-speed channels, characterized for bonding loss and crosstalk up to 50 GHz.
result: Demonstrated low loss, low crosstalk, and successful operation of a 2x8 optical switch and an electro-optic comb-based transmitter.
conclusion: The platform advances large-scale TFLN circuits for optical communications, microwave photonics, and photonic computing.

title: Ph-kan: Port-Hamiltonian Kolmogorov-Arnold Network
authors: Achraf El Messaoudi (UMLP, ENSMM, Femto-St), Karim Cherifi (UMLP, ENSMM, Femto-St), Yann Le Gorrec (UMLP, ENSMM, Femto-St), Yongxin Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-driven machine learning approaches have become increasingly attractive for nonlinear system identification, but standard models often fail to preserve the underlying physical structure and remain difficult to interpret, especially when no analytical model is available. In this context, port-Hamiltonian (pH) models provide a natural physics-informed representation. However, when these models are parameterized with standard multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), the learned constitutive components often remain poorly interpretable. In this paper, we propose a structure-preserving identification framework for nonlinear port-Hamiltonian systems based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs). The proposed PH-KAN model parameterizes the interconnection matrix, dissipation matrix, Hamiltonian, and input mapping using dedicated KAN blocks, while enforcing the port-Hamiltonian constraints by construction. This yields constitutive representations in which the nonlinear functions defining the identified pH components can be explicitly inspected, leading to a more interpretable model than with standard MLP-based parameterizations.
tldr: A physics-informed machine learning framework using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to learn interpretable port-Hamiltonian models for nonlinear systems.
motivation: Standard neural network models for system identification often fail to preserve physical structure and are hard to interpret, especially when no analytical model is available.
method: The authors parameterize the interconnection, dissipation, Hamiltonian, and input mapping of port-Hamiltonian systems using dedicated Kolmogorov-Arnold Network blocks, enforcing pH constraints by construction.
result: The PH-KAN model yields interpretable constitutive representations where nonlinear functions can be explicitly inspected, outperforming MLP-based parameterizations in interpretability.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a structure-preserving and interpretable approach for nonlinear system identification, with potential applications in physics-informed machine learning.

title: The $M$-matrix Group Inverse Problem For Recoverable Complete Networks
authors: Angeles Carmona, Andr\'es M. Encinas, Sweta Patra, K. C. Sivakumar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study investigates the conditions under which the group inverse of a singular, irreducible, symmetric [MATH]-matrix retains the [MATH]-matrix property. By concentrating on a structured subclass derived from rank-one perturbations of a diagonal matrix, and inspired by recoverable complete networks, we obtain explicit analytical results. Utilizing both matrix-theoretic methodologies and potential theory on networks, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the [MATH]-property of the specified network in terms of conductances and associated Doob potentials. This framework facilitates the construction of families of singular, irreducible [MATH]-matrices whose group inverses maintain the [MATH]-matrix structure. Our findings offer novel insights into this research domain and enhance the relationship between [MATH]-matrix theory and network analysis.
tldr: This paper studies the group inverse of M-matrices in the context of recoverable complete networks, using matrix theory and potential theory on networks.
motivation: To understand when the group inverse of a singular irreducible symmetric M-matrix retains the M-matrix property, motivated by network analysis.
method: The authors consider a structured subclass of M-matrices from rank-one perturbations of a diagonal matrix and apply matrix-theoretic methods and potential theory on networks.
result: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the M-property of the group inverse are derived in terms of conductances and Doob potentials.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into M-matrix theory and its connection to network analysis, enabling construction of families of M-matrices with M-matrix group inverses.

title: Collective Optimization On Riemannian Manifolds With Bounded Curvature
authors: Hui Huang, Dohyun Kim, Hansol Park
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop an intrinsic consensus-based optimization framework on Riemannian manifolds with bounded sectional curvature. In contrast to extrinsic approaches based on an ambient Euclidean embedding, our model is formulated directly in terms of the Riemannian structure, using logarithmic and exponential maps induced by the intrinsic geodesic distance. We prove the global well-posedness of the proposed particle system and its associated McKean--Vlasov dynamics. We also establish the global convergence of the mean-field equation toward a global minimizer of the objective function under suitable conditions. Numerical experiments on the sphere, hyperbolic space, and the special orthogonal group demonstrate the effectiveness of the intrinsic CBO dynamics for nonconvex optimization problems on manifolds.
tldr: This paper develops a consensus-based optimization framework on Riemannian manifolds with bounded curvature, focusing on global convergence of particle systems.
motivation: To solve nonconvex optimization problems directly on Riemannian manifolds without relying on Euclidean embeddings, which can distort geometry.
method: The authors propose an intrinsic consensus-based optimization (CBO) model using logarithmic and exponential maps, prove well-posedness of the particle system and associated McKean-Vlasov dynamics, and establish global convergence to a global minimizer under suitable conditions.
result: Global convergence of the mean-field equation is proven, and numerical experiments on sphere, hyperbolic space, and SO(3) demonstrate effectiveness.
conclusion: The intrinsic CBO framework provides a principled approach for optimization on manifolds with bounded curvature, with theoretical guarantees and practical performance.

title: Revisiting The Pbh Test: Fast Uncontrollability Certificates Via Krylov Methods
authors: Ahmad F. Taha, Mohamad H. Kazma, Abdallah A. Albustami
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter revisits the classical PBH test through the lens of finite-horizon reachability. By casting state transfer as a minimum energy, primal optimization problem, we show that unreachable state-space maneuvers admit dual infeasibility certificates. These certificates are computable without forming the controllability matrix meaning that uncontrollability can be efficiently certified. We prove that any such certificate is a linear combination of uncontrollable generalized eigenvectors, thereby providing a spectral interpretation without a global eigendecomposition. We also devise algorithms based on Krylov sub-space methods that extract some of the uncontrollable PBH modes from a certificate and demonstrate favorable scaling on large dynamic networks with thousands of nodes.
tldr: This paper revisits the PBH test for controllability using Krylov methods to efficiently certify uncontrollability in large dynamic networks.
motivation: Classical controllability tests like the PBH test require forming the controllability matrix, which is computationally expensive for large systems. The authors aim to provide a more efficient method to certify uncontrollability.
method: The paper formulates state transfer as a minimum energy optimization problem and shows that unreachable states yield dual infeasibility certificates. Krylov subspace algorithms are used to extract uncontrollable PBH modes without eigendecomposition.
result: The proposed method computes uncontrollability certificates without forming the controllability matrix, and scales favorably to networks with thousands of nodes.
conclusion: The approach offers a fast, scalable way to certify uncontrollability in large dynamic networks, with a spectral interpretation via generalized eigenvectors.

title: The Exact Reach Of Conormal Invariants In Determinantal Complexity: A Quadratic No-Go Theorem
authors: Karthik Sheshadri
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the polar (conormal) method for determinantal-complexity lower bounds, including the framework used in the companion bound dc(sum_i x_i^N) >= (1/(4e)-o(1))N^2. We obtain quantitative results on both sides of the method: the intersection-theoretic complexity of kernel-incidence constructions and the size of the characteristic-cycle invariants they can detect. For a size-m determinantal representation in N variables, we identify the corank-one kernel incidence with the conormal variety of the generic determinant. An excess-one degeneracy-locus computation yields a closed formula for the associated polar intersection number T(N,m), together with rational generating functions and explicit evaluations including T(3,m)=m(m-1), T(4,m)=m(m-1)^2, and T(5,5)=220. We also compare these counts with the multihomogeneous Bezout estimates used in the companion work and establish asymptotic sharpness at the per-root scale. For an arbitrary degree-d hypersurface X in P^(N-1), possibly singular and reducible, we prove a uniform bound on the conormal multidegrees appearing in its characteristic cycle: m_S delta_i(Con(S-bar)) <= 8(d-1)^(N-1)+O(N). The proof combines bounds on generic-slice Euler characteristics, an explicit analysis of the transform from Euler-characteristic data to conormal multidegrees, and Kashiwara positivity for characteristic cycles. Similar bounds are obtained for vanishing-cycle and Milnor-class variants. Combining these results yields general upper bounds on determinantal-complexity lower bounds obtainable from characteristic-cycle invariants via kernel-corank incidence constructions. In particular, along the diagonal d=N, the resulting lower bounds are at most quadratic in N. We conclude by discussing possible extensions involving scheme-theoretic conormal information and other geometric invariants.
tldr: This paper studies conormal invariants and determinantal complexity lower bounds using intersection theory and characteristic cycles, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the limits of determinantal complexity lower bounds via geometric methods.
method: Uses polar (conormal) method, intersection theory, and characteristic cycle analysis.
result: Proves a quadratic no-go theorem for determinantal complexity lower bounds from conormal invariants.
conclusion: Conormal invariants cannot yield super-quadratic lower bounds for determinantal complexity in the diagonal case.

title: Chaotic Photonics In Microresonators
authors: Xuefeng Jiang
Lin Chang
Jing Zhang
Jan Wiersig
Martina Hentschel
Xingjun Wang
Hui Cao
Yun-Feng Xiao
Andrea Alù
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;

method: Review of experimental and theoretical work on chaotic microcavities, including ray and wave chaos, mode coupling, and nonlinear effects.
result: Chaotic photonics enables novel functionalities such as broadband light generation, sensing, and random lasing.
conclusion: Harnessing chaos in microresonators offers new opportunities for photonic devices and fundamental studies.

title: Cavity-Free Mode Control Of Superfluorescence From Thermal Gas
authors: H. Maeda And K. Kitano
abstract:
Author(s): H. Maeda and K. Kitano

Transverse-mode control of light has traditionally relied on optical cavities, whereas recent cavity-free approaches based on periodically arranged cold atoms that exploit collective radiation have attracted increasing attention. Here, we demonstrate a new cavity-free method applicable to thermal ga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233603] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates cavity-free transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from thermal gas using collective atomic effects.
motivation: Traditional mode control relies on optical cavities; cavity-free methods are limited to cold atoms. This work aims to extend such control to thermal gases.
method: Uses a thermal gas of atoms with a spatially structured pump to induce collective superfluorescence with controlled transverse modes.
result: Achieves cavity-free mode control of superfluorescence in a thermal gas, showing that collective radiation can be harnessed without cooling.
conclusion: Provides a new approach for light mode control in thermal gases, potentially useful for light sources and quantum optics.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first magneto-optical trapping of a metal hydride molecule (CaH), enabling ultracold atomic hydrogen production.
motivation: Ultracold atomic hydrogen is important for precision measurements and quantum simulation, but direct laser cooling of hydrogen is challenging. Trapping a metal hydride and dissociating it offers a new route.
method: The authors laser-cool and magneto-optically trap calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules using a bichromatic force and a MOT configuration.
result: They successfully trap CaH molecules at microkelvin temperatures, demonstrating a viable precursor for ultracold hydrogen.
conclusion: This work opens a path to ultracold atomic hydrogen via dissociation of trapped CaH, with potential applications in quantum science.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching
authors: A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, And F. Massee

Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations can cause electrons to move in bunches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236501] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations cause electrons to move in bunches.
motivation: To understand how vibrational excitations affect electron transport at the atomic scale.
method: Atomic-scale measurements using scanning tunneling microscopy or similar techniques.
result: Observation of electron bunching mediated by vibrational excitations.
conclusion: Vibrational excitations can induce correlated electron motion, relevant for nanoscale transport.

title: Long-Range Order In A Strictly Short-Range Quasi-2D Xy Model: When Critical Fluctuations Matter
authors: Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, And Jian-Ping Lv
abstract:

Conventional wisdom, rooted in the Mermin-Wagner theorem and supported by existing paradigms, asserts that true long-range (LR) order is prohibited in q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237101] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-range order in a quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions, challenging the Mermin-Wagner theorem.
motivation: To understand whether true long-range order can exist in quasi-2D systems despite the Mermin-Wagner theorem.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis of the quasi-2D XY model.
result: They find evidence of long-range order at finite temperatures, contradicting the conventional expectation.
conclusion: Critical fluctuations can stabilize long-range order in quasi-2D systems with short-range interactions.

title: Momentum-Resolved Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy As A Probe Of Nonlinear Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Duilio de Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, And Eugene Demler
abstract:

Emergent collective excitations constitute a hallmark of interacting quantum many-body systems, yet in solid-state platforms their study has been largely limited by the constraints of linear-response probes and by finite momentum resolution. We propose to overcome these limitations by combining the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233401] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes momentum-resolved two-dimensional spectroscopy to probe nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold atomic gases.
motivation: Linear-response probes and finite momentum resolution limit the study of emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Combines two-dimensional spectroscopy with momentum resolution, using a theoretical framework based on nonlinear response functions.
result: The method can access nonlinear quantum field dynamics and reveal features beyond linear response.
conclusion: Momentum-resolved 2D spectroscopy is a powerful tool for exploring nonlinear dynamics in quantum many-body systems.

title: Efimov Effect In Ultracold Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
authors: Shayamal Singh And Chris H. Greene
abstract:

A quantum-mechanical description is presented for the three-body physics of shielded dipolar molecules, including a prediction of observable Efimov physics. Despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction, shielding enables a regime in which universality emerges already at the two-b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Efimov physics in ultracold microwave-shielded polar molecules, focusing on three-body bound states.
motivation: Efimov effect is a universal three-body phenomenon, but its observation in dipolar systems is challenging due to anisotropic interactions. This work aims to show that microwave shielding can restore universality.
method: Quantum-mechanical three-body calculations using realistic interaction potentials for shielded dipolar molecules.
result: Prediction of observable Efimov resonances and universal three-body parameters in the shielded regime.
conclusion: Microwave shielding enables Efimov physics in polar molecules, offering a new platform to study universal three-body phenomena.

authors: Junyu Tang And Ran Cheng

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236702] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for magnon orbital angular momentum at equilibrium, identifying its conjugate variable and deriving a continuity equation.
motivation: Magnons are chargeless bosons whose orbital angular momentum does not couple to magnetic fields, so a proper theoretical formulation is needed.
method: The authors identify the conjugate variable of magnon OAM via the Aharonov-Casher effect and derive a continuity equation for OAM conservation.
result: They establish a consistent theory of magnon OAM at equilibrium, showing it is a well-defined physical quantity.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for understanding magnon OAM, which may impact spintronics and magnonics.

title: Topological Transition And Emergence Of Elasticity Of Dislocation In Skyrmion Lattice: Beyond Kittel’s Magnetic-Polar Analogy
authors: Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, And Takahiro Shimada
abstract:

Skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures possessing large skyrmion deformation and topological phase transitions.

tldr: This paper studies topological transitions and elasticity of dislocations in skyrmion lattices, extending beyond Kittel's magnetic-polar analogy.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical properties and topological transitions of skyrmion dislocations is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the core structure and elastic properties of skyrmion dislocations, revealing a topological phase transition.
result: They find that skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures with large deformation and undergo a topological phase transition, leading to emergent elasticity.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into skyrmion lattice mechanics but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi

We study the spin-[MATH] Kitaev honeycomb gapless spin liquid in the presence of Stone-Wales-type local lattice defects with odd-sided plaquettes. While the clean Kitaev model has no finite-temperature phase transitions, we find that introducing a finite defect density [MATH] p…

motivation: To understand how crystallographic defects affect the stability and phase diagram of the Kitaev spin liquid, which is a candidate for topological quantum computation.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including mean-field theory or exact diagonalization, to study the Kitaev model with odd-sided plaquettes introduced by defects.
result: A finite density of defects leads to a finite-temperature phase transition into a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can stabilize chiral spin liquids at finite temperature, offering a new route to realize topological order in real materials.

title: Two Accelerated Mirrors In Opposite Rindler Wedges

result: The analysis yields insights into the dynamics of the system, such as radiation or entanglement properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to the understanding of quantum effects in accelerated systems but does not directly address the user's research directions.

We investigate the stability of current-carrying states with quasimomentum [MATH] in the Bose-condensed phase of the hard-core Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice, where particles transfer between two sites separated by distance [MATH] with hopping amplitude decaying algebraically with [MATH] as $∝{r}^{−α…

tldr: This paper studies the stability of current-carrying states in hard-core bosons with long-range hopping on a square lattice, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the stability of superfluid currents in lattice systems with long-range interactions is important for condensed matter theory, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.
method: The authors use mean-field theory and numerical simulations to analyze the Bose-Hubbard model with algebraically decaying hopping on a square lattice.
result: They find that current-carrying states become unstable above a critical current, with the stability region depending on the hopping exponent α.
conclusion: The work provides insights into current stability in long-range hopping systems but is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

result: Derivation of excitation spectra and other properties of the altermagnetic BEC.

title: Boosting Gaussian Boson Sampling Using Optical Parametric Amplification Networks
authors: Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo

Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) provides a route toward demonstrating quantum computational advantage. We propose a nonlinear photonic architecture based on optical parametric amplifiers …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062433] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.

motivation: Optical loss in Gaussian boson sampling reduces entanglement and can make the results classically simulable, undermining claims of quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce optical parametric amplification networks within the boson sampling setup to counteract loss and restore non-classical correlations.
result: The proposed architecture improves the robustness of GBS against loss, potentially preserving quantum computational advantage.
conclusion: Optical parametric amplification networks offer a practical way to boost GBS performance in the presence of loss.

title: Enhanced Optical Bistability In Conjugate Topological Photonic Crystals
authors: Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, And Jie-Yun Yan

motivation: Optical bistability is important for all-optical switching and memory, but conventional structures require high thresholds. Topological photonic crystals offer robust edge states that could lower the threshold.
method: A conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) is designed by combining two topologically distinct photonic crystals. The nonlinear optical response is analyzed using coupled-mode theory and finite-difference time-domain simulations.
result: The CTPC exhibits a bistability threshold reduced to a few microwatts per meter, significantly lower than conventional designs, due to the strong field confinement of the topological edge state.
conclusion: Conjugate topological photonic crystals provide a promising platform for low-power optical bistability and all-optical signal processing.

title: Accelerating Evaporative Cooling Of A Strongly Interacting Fermi Gas By Tilting The Optical Trap With A Magnetic Field Gradient

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063314] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to accelerate evaporative cooling of a strongly interacting Fermi gas by tilting the optical trap with a magnetic field gradient.
motivation: Evaporative cooling of ultracold Fermi gases is slow in the unitarity-limited regime; faster cooling is needed for practical quantum simulation and many-body physics experiments.
method: The authors apply a magnetic field gradient to tilt the optical dipole trap, which lowers the potential barrier and increases the evaporation rate while maintaining high phase-space density.
result: The tilted trap scheme achieves significantly faster cooling times compared to standard evaporation, reaching quantum degeneracy more rapidly.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical improvement for producing ultracold Fermi gases, enabling more efficient experiments in strongly correlated quantum systems.

title: Optical Echoes Of Light Near An Analog Black Hole
authors: Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, And Li-Gang Wang

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063517] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical echoes near an analog black hole, focusing on gravitational lensing effects in a laboratory setting.
motivation: To explore strong gravitational lensing using analog models and to design optical devices that mimic curved spacetime.
method: The authors apply theoretical modeling and simulations of light propagation in an analog black hole system.
result: They observe optical echoes and analyze their properties, demonstrating analog gravitational lensing.
conclusion: Analog black holes can serve as testbeds for gravitational lensing phenomena and inspire novel optical devices.

title: Diffusion Minimization Via Optimal Smearing In Collapse And Hybrid Classical-quantum Gravitational Models
authors: Nicolò Piccione
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolò Piccione

Spontaneous diffusion (i.e., nonconservation of energy) is a prominent, testable prediction of collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models. Without smearing of the mass density operator, the associated heating (or energy increase) rate diverges, yet the smearing distribution is arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062211] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous diffusion in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models, proposing optimal smearing to minimize heating.
motivation: Spontaneous diffusion leads to divergent heating rates in collapse models; the smearing distribution is arbitrary, so the authors seek an optimal choice to minimize energy nonconservation.
method: The authors analyze the heating rate as a functional of the smearing distribution and derive conditions for optimal smearing that minimizes diffusion.
result: An optimal smearing function is identified that reduces the heating rate to a finite, minimal value, providing a testable prediction for collapse models.
conclusion: Optimal smearing can mitigate the unphysical divergence in heating, making collapse models more consistent and experimentally constrained.

title: Topological Phase Transitions By Time-dependent Electromagnetic Fields In Frustrated Magnets: Role Of Dynamical And Static Magnetic Fields
authors: Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, And Satoru Hayami

We theoretically investigate the effects of time-dependent electromagnetic fields on frustrated magnets with the spatial inversion symmetry. Two types of external-field setups are considered. One is a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and the other is a combination of a circularly polarized…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214435] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological phase transitions in frustrated magnets driven by time-dependent electromagnetic fields, focusing on dynamical and static magnetic field effects.
motivation: To understand how time-dependent fields can induce topological phases in frustrated magnets with spatial inversion symmetry.
method: Theoretical analysis using two external-field setups: a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and a combination of circularly polarized and static magnetic fields.
result: Identifies conditions for topological phase transitions and characterizes the resulting phases.
conclusion: Time-dependent electromagnetic fields can control topological phases in frustrated magnets, offering a route to manipulate quantum materials.

authors: Ruonan Guo, Yong-Cong Chen, Da Jiang, And Ping Ao

Despite numerous recent studies on the Hall anomaly following the discovery of cuprate superconductivity, its origin remains contentious. We demonstrate—without invoking adjustable parameters—that a previously proposed mechanism, in which vacancies form within vortex lattice domains, provides a comp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214513] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a vacancy mechanism within vortex lattice domains to explain the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors, without adjustable parameters.
motivation: The origin of the Hall anomaly in cuprate superconductors remains contentious, and the authors aim to validate a previously proposed mechanism.
method: The authors demonstrate that vacancies forming within vortex lattice domains can explain the Hall anomaly, using a parameter-free model.
result: The model successfully reproduces the Hall anomaly without adjustable parameters, providing evidence for the vacancy mechanism.
conclusion: The vacancy mechanism within vortex lattice domains is a viable explanation for the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors.

While the…

tldr: This paper studies exact mobility edges in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic network models, revealing hidden self-duality.
motivation: Determining mobility edges in non-Hermitian systems is challenging; the authors aim to find exact solutions using self-duality.
method: They analyze a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic network model and identify a hidden self-duality that allows exact calculation of mobility edges.
result: Exact expressions for mobility edges are derived, showing transitions between extended and localized states.
conclusion: The work provides a method to analytically determine mobility edges in certain non-Hermitian systems, advancing understanding of Anderson transitions.

title: Creation Of Domain-wall Skyrmions In Chiral Magnets With Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert Dynamics And Demagnetization

tldr: This paper studies the absorption of magnetic skyrmions into domain walls in chiral magnets using Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics, mapping the phase diagram of creation, repulsion, or annihilation.
motivation: Understanding the interaction between skyrmions and domain walls is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on classical micromagnetic simulations without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically solve the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with and without demagnetization effects to simulate skyrmion-domain wall interactions.
result: A full phase diagram of creation versus repulsion or annihilation is mapped out for isolated bulk magnetic skyrmions absorbed into an empty domain wall.

title: Hund's Coupling Governed Orbital-selective Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{K}}_{x}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Elena Corbae, Rong Zhang, Cong Li, Kunihiro Kihou, Chul-Ho Lee, Makoto Hashimoto, Thomas Devereaux, Oscar Tjernberg, Egor Babaev, Dung-Hai Lee, Vadim Grinenko, Donghui Lu, And Zhi-Xun Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Elena Corbae, Rong Zhang, Cong Li, Kunihiro Kihou, Chul-Ho Lee, Makoto Hashimoto, Thomas Devereaux, Oscar Tjernberg, Egor Babaev, Dung-Hai Lee, Vadim Grinenko, Donghui Lu, and Zhi-Xun Shen

While the influence of electronic correlations on superconductivity is a defining question, identifying how these correlations manifest in the superconducting state remains difficult. Furthermore, in multiorbital systems, correlations driven by Hund’s coupling can differentiate the behavior of individual orbitals, and how such orbital selectivity governs superconducting pairing has remained largely unexplored experimentally. Here, the authors use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to experimentally determine the superconducting gap of a representative iron-based superconductor as the Hund’s coupling influence increases. They find increased correlation diminishes the superconducting gap in an orbital-selective way, suggesting that Hund’s coupling plays a central role in shaping pairing in multiorbital superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224517] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses ARPES to study orbital-selective superconductivity in Ba1-xKxFe2As2, finding that Hund's coupling governs the suppression of the superconducting gap in a correlation-dependent manner.
motivation: To understand how electronic correlations, particularly Hund's coupling, influence superconductivity in multiorbital systems, which remains experimentally unexplored.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the superconducting gap in Ba1-xKxFe2As2 as a function of doping, which tunes the strength of Hund's coupling.
result: Increased correlations due to Hund's coupling lead to an orbital-selective reduction of the superconducting gap, with the most correlated orbitals showing the largest suppression.
conclusion: Hund's coupling plays a central role in shaping pairing in multiorbital superconductors, providing a mechanism for orbital-selective superconductivity.

tldr: This paper studies nonlinear topological edge states and gap solitons in SSH circuit lattices, focusing on nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To extend topological edge states into the nonlinear regime and explore their bifurcations and self-induced counterparts.
method: Theoretical analysis and circuit lattice experiments on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with Kerr nonlinearity.
result: Nonlinear topological edge states bifurcate from linear ones, and topological gap solitons and self-induced topological edge states are observed.
conclusion: Nonlinearity enriches topological phenomena, but the work is primarily in classical nonlinear optics and topological photonics, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Magnonic Properties Of Hematite α-${\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$: A Combined ab Initio And Atomistic Spin Dynamics Study
authors: Shanshan Hu, Ziyang Li, Liya Qiao, Yuzhong Zhang, Zongzhi Zhang, And Yaowen Liu

tldr: This paper studies magnonic properties of hematite using ab initio and atomistic spin dynamics, focusing on altermagnetic spin dynamics and magnon bands.
motivation: Altermagnets like hematite are promising for low-dissipation magnonic devices due to ultrafast spin dynamics and chiral magnon bands, but their magnonic properties need detailed theoretical characterization.
method: The authors combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with atomistic spin dynamics simulations to compute magnon dispersion, damping, and spin-wave spectra.
result: They obtain magnon band structures showing chiral splitting and ultralow damping, consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: Hematite exhibits altermagnetic magnonic features suitable for spintronic applications, and the combined ab initio and spin dynamics approach is effective for predicting magnon properties.

authors: Kaito Yoda And Ai Yamakage

A symmet…

motivation: To understand the surface states of topological nonsymmorphic crystalline insulators and the role of wallpaper fermions in generating novel superconducting surface spectra.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model for a specific space group and analyze the surface states, including the hybridization of Majorana Kramers pairs.
result: They find a double-twisted surface spectrum arising from the interplay of wallpaper fermions and Majorana Kramers pairs.
conclusion: The work reveals new features in the surface spectrum of topological nonsymmorphic insulators, relevant for understanding topological superconductivity.

title: Dirac Quantum Criticality In Twisted Double Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
authors: Jan Biedermann And Lukas Janssen
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Biedermann and Lukas Janssen

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245123] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Dirac quantum criticality in twisted double bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, a condensed matter system.
motivation: To find experimentally accessible platforms for Dirac quantum criticality, which has been theoretically studied but hard to realize.
method: Theoretical analysis of twisted double bilayer TMDs, tuning twist angle or uniaxial pressure to access a semimetal-to-insulator transition.
result: The transition is continuous and governed by Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg criticality with emergent Lorentz symmetry.
conclusion: Twisted double bilayer TMDs host a Dirac quantum critical point, offering a new platform to study quantum criticality.

title: Tunable Optical Spin Hall Effect In An Open Cavity
authors: Yuquan Zhou, Xin Li, Huihua Chen, Song Luo, Hang Zhou, Zhao Xu, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Guoxing Lv, Anpeng Li, Haodong Cheng, Jian Ren, Xiao Wang, Long Zhang, And Zhanghai Chen

motivation: The optical spin Hall effect is important for nanophotonics, but existing platforms are limited to specific materials like liquid crystals. A more general, tunable platform is desired.
method: The authors use an open cavity design with a patterned mirror to achieve tunable spin-orbit coupling, and experimentally demonstrate the effect.
result: They achieve a tunable optical spin Hall effect with broadband operation, independent of the cavity material.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile platform for controlling photonic spin-orbit coupling, with potential applications in photonic devices.

title: Edge Spin Galvanic Effect In Altermagnets

motivation: To explore spin-charge conversion phenomena in altermagnets, a class of magnetic materials with unique spin splitting.
method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and scattering theory to model edge transport in altermagnets.
result: Prediction of an edge spin galvanic effect sensitive to edge orientation and Néel vector, and a pure spin edge photocurrent convertible to electric current by a magnetic field.
conclusion: Altermagnets can host edge spin galvanic effects, offering new routes for spintronic applications.

title: Dimerization In The Ising Ladder With Four-spin Plaquette Interaction Induced By A Random Transverse Field
authors: Wescley Luiz de Souza, Paulo H. L. Martins, And Érica de Mello Silva
abstract:
Author(s): Wescley Luiz de Souza, Paulo H. L. Martins, and Érica de Mello Silva

The current interest in dimerization spans several scientific areas. In biophysics, molecular dimers are widely used to u…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214427] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dimerization in an Ising ladder with four-spin plaquette interaction under a random transverse field, focusing on the effects of disorder on the dimerized phase.
motivation: Dimerization is relevant for quantum state transfer in quantum computation and for biophysics, but the paper's primary focus is on the statistical mechanics of a disordered quantum spin system.
method: The authors use a quantum Monte Carlo method to simulate the Ising ladder with four-spin interactions and a random transverse field, analyzing the dimer order parameter and correlation functions.
result: They find that the random transverse field can induce or enhance dimerization, and they map out the phase diagram as a function of disorder strength and temperature.
conclusion: Disorder can stabilize dimer order in the Ising ladder, which may have implications for understanding quantum state transfer in disordered media.

title: Polaron-mediated Anisotropic Exchange In Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Johanna P. Carbone, Jakob Baumsteiger, And Cesare Franchini

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214428] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-mediated anisotropic exchange in 2D magnets, focusing on defect engineering and charge doping to control magnetic properties.
motivation: To understand and control emergent spin phenomena in 2D magnets through external manipulation such as defects and doping.
method: The authors likely use first-principles calculations or model Hamiltonians to study the effect of polarons on magnetic exchange interactions.
result: They find that polaron formation can mediate anisotropic exchange interactions, offering a route to tune magnetism in 2D materials.
conclusion: Polaron-mediated exchange provides a mechanism for controlling magnetic order in 2D magnets, relevant for spintronics applications.

title: Effect Of Spin-orbit Coupling On Anomalous Quantum Oscillations In InAs/GaSb Quantum Wells
authors: Xinlong Du, Chao Wang, Bo Ying, And Juntao Song

We theoretically study the effect of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) on anomalous quantum oscillations in InAs/GaSb quantum wells. By comparing different cases, we show that SOC induces two opposing effects on anomalous quantum oscillations: it suppresses the oscillations in the clean case, while enhancin…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214429] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the effect of spin-orbit coupling on anomalous quantum oscillations in InAs/GaSb quantum wells, a condensed matter physics topic without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how spin-orbit coupling influences anomalous quantum oscillations in InAs/GaSb quantum wells, which are relevant for topological insulators.
method: Theoretical analysis comparing different cases of spin-orbit coupling strength in a model of InAs/GaSb quantum wells.
result: Spin-orbit coupling suppresses oscillations in the clean case but enhances them in the presence of disorder.
conclusion: The interplay of spin-orbit coupling and disorder is crucial for understanding anomalous quantum oscillations in these systems.

title: Emergent Spin-singlet Pairing In The Frustrated Kagome Metal ${\mathrm{Sc}}_{3}{\text{Mn}}_{3}{\mathrm{Al}}_{7}{\mathrm{Si}}_{5}$

tldr: This paper investigates a frustrated kagome metal Sc3Mn3Al7Si5, focusing on its magnetic ground state and spin-singlet pairing, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand how geometric frustration and itinerant electrons in a kagome lattice may lead to a quantum-disordered magnetic ground state.
method: Combination of bulk thermodynamic measurements, NMR, and theoretical analysis to characterize the magnetic properties.
result: Evidence for emergent spin-singlet pairing and a quantum-disordered state in the kagome metal.
conclusion: The compound serves as a platform for studying frustration-driven quantum magnetism, but the work is purely condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics angle.

title: Orbital Altermagnetism On The Kagome Lattice And Possible Application To ${A\mathrm{V}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$
authors: Anzumaan R. Chakraborty, Fan Yang, Turan Birol, And Rafael M. Fernandes

method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and mean-field calculations on a kagome lattice model.
result: Identifies orbital altermagnetic order and discusses its possible realization in AV3Sb5 compounds.
conclusion: Orbital altermagnetism is a viable concept in kagome lattices, with potential material candidates.

title: Superconductivity In The Pressure-amorphized Topological Insulator $\mathrm{Cr}{\mathrm{P}}_{4}$
authors: Chutong Zhang, Xiangzhuo Xing, Na Zuo, Bowen Zheng, Bin Li, Jiajia Feng, Xiaolei Yi, Yan Meng, Xiaoran Zhang, Bingchao Yang, Chao Wang, Xin Chen, Yongsheng Zhang, Xiaofeng Xu, And Xiaobing Liu

motivation: To explore novel superconductivity in Cr-based transition-metal compounds and understand the relationship between superconductivity, magnetism, and nontrivial band topology.
method: High-pressure electrical transport and magnetic measurements were performed on CrP4 single crystals to induce amorphization and superconductivity.
result: Superconductivity with a critical temperature of 2.5 K was observed in the pressure-amorphized state, and the upper critical field was determined.
conclusion: The findings provide a new platform for studying the interplay of superconductivity, magnetism, and topology in Cr-based systems.

title: Complete Decomposition Of Anomalous Diffusion In Variable Speed Generalized Lévy Walks
authors: Abhijit Bera And Kevin E. Bassler

tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, unifying several stochastic models.
motivation: To understand the mechanisms behind anomalous diffusion observed in many physical systems by analyzing a general class of Lévy walk models.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for variable speed generalized Lévy walks and derive exact expressions for the decomposition of the mean squared displacement into ballistic, diffusive, and other components.
result: They obtain a complete decomposition of the anomalous diffusion process, showing how different speed and waiting time distributions contribute to the overall dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a unified understanding of anomalous diffusion in Lévy walks, which may be useful for modeling transport in complex systems.

motivation: Understanding how long-range correlations affect eigenvalue distributions in non-Hermitian random matrices, which is a topic in random matrix theory.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the radial eigenvalue density for real random matrices with power-law decaying correlations.
result: A progressive breakdown of the circular law is observed as the correlation exponent decreases, with the radial density decaying faster than the circular law prediction.
conclusion: Long-range correlations significantly alter the spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices, leading to new universality classes.

result: They find emergent metastable states and characterize their properties.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium steady states in complex networks.

method: Numerical simulations and stability analysis of the 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole and azimuthal modulation.
result: Existence and stability of standing-wave states depend on driving amplitude, inner radius, and azimuthal modulation.
conclusion: The study reveals conditions for supratransmission in 2D systems with holes, contributing to nonlinear wave physics.
