abstract: ArXiv:2606.15634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we address the channel estimation (CE) problem in SIM-based multi-user (MU) millimeter-wave (mmWave) near-field communication systems. To address the severe path loss and blockage in mmWave communication systems, many meta-atoms are typically integrated into each layer of the SIM. Then, the number of radio frequency (RF) chains at the base station (BS) is fewer than that of meta-atoms per layer, resulting in an underdetermined problem. Additionally, the increase in the number of meta-atoms in each layer expands the SIM's near-field region, leading to the user equipment (UEs) being mostly situated in this region, necessitating precise modeling of the channel under the spherical wavefront assumption. To address these issues, we introduce a compressed sensing (CS)-based CE protocol to tackle the underdetermined problem. In contrast to the traditional CS-based estimation framework, we investigate a polar-domain channel representation to tackle the severe energy spread effect of the classical angular-domain channel representation in near-field communication systems. Specifically, we design a novel polar-domain transform matrix for uniform planar arrays (UPAs), thereby transforming the CE problem into a sparse recovery task of the paths' support set and complex gains. To overcome the limitations of the sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) framework in tackling high-dimensional dictionaries, we propose a low-complexity polar-domain SBL (LCPD-SBL) algorithm, which significantly reduces computational complexity without compromising estimation accuracy.
tldr: This paper proposes a sparse channel estimation method for SIM-based millimeter-wave near-field communications using a polar-domain transform and a low-complexity sparse Bayesian learning algorithm.
motivation: The paper addresses the underdetermined channel estimation problem in SIM-based multi-user mmWave near-field systems, where the number of RF chains is fewer than meta-atoms per layer, and the near-field region requires spherical wavefront modeling.
method: The authors introduce a compressed sensing-based CE protocol with a novel polar-domain transform matrix for uniform planar arrays to achieve sparse representation, and propose a low-complexity polar-domain sparse Bayesian learning (LCPD-SBL) algorithm to solve the sparse recovery problem.
result: The LCPD-SBL algorithm significantly reduces computational complexity without compromising estimation accuracy compared to standard SBL.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively handles the underdetermined CE problem in SIM-based mmWave near-field communications, enabling practical implementation.

title: AnonShield: Scalable On-Premise Pseudonymization For Csirt Vulnerability Data
authors: Cristhian Kapelinski, Douglas Lautert, Beatriz Machado, Diego Kreutz, Isadora Garcia Ferr\~ao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present AnonShield, a high-throughput, on-premise pseudonymization system that combines GPU-accelerated NER, streaming processing, caching, and schema-aware configuration. Evaluated on datasets up to 550 MB (70,951 records), AnonShield reduces processing time from over 92 hours to under 10 minutes (up to 738x speedup) while achieving up to 94.2% F1-score and 96.7% recall. Our results show that scalable pseudonymization of vulnerability data is feasible without sacrificing analytical utility, enabling compliant data sharing in operational CSIRT environments.
tldr: AnonShield is a GPU-accelerated pseudonymization system for CSIRT vulnerability data, achieving high throughput and accuracy.
motivation: CSIRTs need to share vulnerability data while preserving privacy, but existing pseudonymization tools are too slow for large datasets.
method: The system combines GPU-accelerated named entity recognition, streaming processing, caching, and schema-aware configuration to pseudonymize records efficiently.
result: On datasets up to 550 MB (70,951 records), processing time reduced from over 92 hours to under 10 minutes (up to 738x speedup) with up to 94.2% F1-score and 96.7% recall.
conclusion: Scalable on-premise pseudonymization of vulnerability data is feasible without sacrificing analytical utility, enabling compliant data sharing in operational CSIRT environments.

title: The Algebra Of Krom Logic Programs
authors: Christian Anti\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the algebraic structure of Krom logic programs, consisting only of facts and rules with at most one body atom. We show that sequential composition endows the class of Krom programs with a natural monoid structure and that this structure admits rich algebraic extensions to Krom seminearrings, Krom quemirings, Krom-Conway seminearrings, and Krom-Conway omegaseminearrings. Furthermore, we establish explicit generating sets and canonical decompositions, study the associated [MATH]-operator, characterize the Kleene star in graph-theoretic terms, and relate finite Krom monoids to transformation monoids and finite-state automata. These results provide new connections between logic programming, algebraic automata theory, and algebraic graph theory.
tldr: This paper studies the algebraic structure of Krom logic programs, establishing monoid, seminearring, and Conway algebra connections to automata theory and graph theory.
motivation: To understand the algebraic foundations of a restricted class of logic programs (Krom programs) and relate them to well-known algebraic structures.
method: The paper defines sequential composition on Krom programs, proves monoid properties, and extends to seminearrings, quemirings, and Conway algebras. It also characterizes the Kleene star graph-theoretically.
result: Krom programs form a monoid under sequential composition, and this structure extends to various algebraic frameworks; generating sets and canonical decompositions are provided.
conclusion: The work bridges logic programming, algebraic automata theory, and algebraic graph theory, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Interpolation And Query Rewriting
authors: Michael Benedikt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We overview applications of Craig interpolation and Beth definability to simplifying logical expressions or database queries. From the perspective of the theory of interpolation and definability the results give a number of new angles. First, they give a different take on what it means to make definability or interpolation results effective, looking at algorithms that take a proof as input and return an interpolant or explicit definition as output. Secondly, they relate interpolation and definability to preservation theorems in model theory: interpolation and definability theorems are the basis for many "semantics-to-syntax" results, relating a semantic property of a formula to its equivalence with a certain syntactic form. Thirdly, they motivate new forms of interpolation and definability, focusing on syntactic forms that are of interest in databases.
tldr: This paper surveys applications of Craig interpolation and Beth definability to simplifying logical expressions and database queries.
motivation: The work aims to connect interpolation and definability theory with database query optimization and simplification.
method: The paper reviews known results and presents new perspectives on effective interpolation algorithms, preservation theorems, and syntactic forms relevant to databases.
result: It highlights how interpolation and definability can be used to rewrite queries into simpler forms and relates these to model-theoretic preservation theorems.
conclusion: The paper provides a conceptual overview rather than new technical results, emphasizing the utility of interpolation in database contexts.

title: Snyk VulnBench Js 1.0: Can LLMs Find The Same Bugs Twice?
authors: Liran Tal, Johannes Kloos, Arsenii Rudich, Stephen Thoemmes, Manoj Nair
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We ran 300 repeated vulnerability-finding scans to measure how repeatable agentic large language model (LLM) security review is on the same JavaScript code, prompt, and benchmark harness. The headline result is that LLM security findings were unevenly repeatable: reference-matched findings were stable, but extra model reports varied heavily from run to run. Across 250 model runs, 80 of 161 unique unmatched findings appeared in only one of five identical repetitions, while only 22 appeared in all five. By contrast, when Claude matched a Snyk Code reference finding, the behavior was much more stable: 134 of 158 unique reference-matched findings appeared in all five repetitions. The benchmark also shows complementarity. Models consistently found familiar, high-signal exploit shapes, and in one case surfaced a likely Snyk Code product gap. Snyk Code static application security testing (SAST) was deterministic and better at systematically enumerating repeated data-flow sinks. The results support combining agentic LLM review with deterministic SAST rather than treating either technique as a replacement for the other.
tldr: This paper evaluates the repeatability of LLM-based security vulnerability detection in JavaScript code, comparing it with deterministic SAST tools.
motivation: To assess whether LLMs can consistently find the same security bugs across repeated runs, and to understand the reliability of agentic LLM security review.
method: 300 repeated vulnerability-finding scans using the same LLM (Claude) on the same JavaScript code, prompt, and benchmark harness, with results compared to Snyk Code SAST.
result: LLM findings were unevenly repeatable: reference-matched findings were stable, but extra model reports varied heavily; SAST was deterministic and better at systematic enumeration.
conclusion: Combining agentic LLM review with deterministic SAST is recommended over treating either as a replacement.

title: GAS-Leak-LLM: Genetic Algorithm-Based Suffix Optimization For Black-Box Llm Jailbreaking
authors: Aman Anifer, Vignesh Kumar Kembu, Vishnu M, Antonino Nocera, Vinod P., Amal Murali PK, Akshay S Rajan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) constitute pivotal components within the AI-dominated information technology ecosystem. To mitigate risks associated with harmful or policy-violating outputs, commercial systems employ advanced alignment strategies and multi-layered content moderation mechanisms. Despite these safeguards, recent research has demonstrated that LLMs remain vulnerable to adversarial manipulation, particularly through jailbreaking and prompt injection techniques. In this work, we propose GAS-Leak-LLM a novel jailbreaking attack based on a genetic algorithm that systematically evolves adversarial suffix to bypass safety constraints. Operating in a strict black-box setting, our method requires no access to model parameters or internals, thereby reflecting realistic threat scenarios in deployed systems. Through the iterative application of selection, mutation, and crossover heuristics, the framework systematically explores the discrete prompt space to identify high-fitness adversarial suffixes. Empirical findings reveal critical shortcomings in existing safety enforcement mechanisms and confirm the effectiveness and practical viability of the proposed attack.
tldr: This paper proposes a genetic algorithm-based jailbreaking attack on LLMs, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: LLMs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that bypass safety constraints, posing security risks in deployed systems.
method: A genetic algorithm evolves adversarial suffixes in a black-box setting using selection, mutation, and crossover to find suffixes that elicit harmful responses.
result: The attack successfully generates adversarial suffixes that bypass safety mechanisms, demonstrating critical shortcomings in current LLM alignment.
conclusion: The proposed method is effective and highlights the need for more robust safety measures in LLMs.

title: AttackonCTF: Defending Hardware Security Competition Benchmarks In The Age Of LLMs
authors: Mohamadreza Rostami, Nikhilesh Singh, Stephen Muttathil, Lichao Wu, Chen Chen, Huimin Li, Jeyavijayan Rajendran, Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware security competitions such as HackTheSilicon serve as benchmarking platforms for evaluating vulnerability detection methods and for training humans and AI. However, our study reveals that LLMs threaten their validity. Instead of genuine security reasoning, detectors exploit a diff-style syntactic comparison, achieving an 83% detection rate, undermining fair evaluation. To mitigate this, we propose the first LLM-oriented, semantics-preserving obfuscation framework for these benchmarks. Unlike IP-protection approaches, it applies human-readable transformations and controlled diff-noise while preserving functionality. On HackTheSilicon, the framework reduces LLM-based detection accuracy by 50% with only 10% obfuscation and by 78.6% under complete obfuscation, restoring benchmark reliability.
tldr: This paper addresses vulnerabilities in hardware security competitions due to LLMs exploiting syntactic comparisons, and proposes an obfuscation framework to restore benchmark reliability.
motivation: Hardware security competitions are used to benchmark vulnerability detection methods, but LLMs can cheat by exploiting diff-style syntactic comparisons rather than genuine security reasoning, undermining fair evaluation.
method: The authors propose a semantics-preserving obfuscation framework that applies human-readable transformations and controlled diff-noise to benchmarks, reducing LLM detection accuracy while preserving functionality.
result: The framework reduces LLM-based detection accuracy by 50% with 10% obfuscation and by 78.6% under complete obfuscation on the HackTheSilicon benchmark.
conclusion: The proposed obfuscation framework effectively mitigates LLM exploitation in hardware security competitions, restoring the validity of these benchmarks.

title: Let Them Steal: Trapping Large Language Model Extraction Attacks With Knowledge Honeypot
authors: Yushun Dong Yuyang Dai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models deployed as commercial APIs are vulnerable to model extraction attacks, while existing defenses either act too late or degrade utility for legitimate users. We propose , a defense that redirects extraction attacks toward low-transferability knowledge through a (HKG) and breadcrumb-guided exploration. Instead of blocking queries or perturbing outputs, Knowledge Trap consumes the attacker's limited query budget on knowledge with negligible downstream utility while preserving benign-user performance. Experiments in medical and financial domains show that Knowledge Trap reduces surrogate Agreement by 6.2\% on average without degrading legitimate-user accuracy, outperforming existing defenses that impose measurable user impact. These results suggest that defending knowledge-space traversal is a practical direction for mitigating LLM extraction attacks.
tldr: Proposes a defense against model extraction attacks on LLMs using a knowledge honeypot.
motivation: Existing defenses against LLM model extraction either degrade utility or act too late.
method: Introduces a Knowledge Trap that redirects attackers to low-transferability knowledge via a honeypot knowledge graph and breadcrumb-guided exploration.
result: Reduces surrogate agreement by 6.2% on average without harming legitimate user accuracy.
conclusion: Defending knowledge-space traversal is a practical direction for mitigating LLM extraction attacks.

title: FuseChain: Runtime Evidence Reconstruction For Software Supply-Chain Attacks
authors: Zhuoran Tan, Yutian Tang, Jeremy Singer, Christos Anagnostopoulos, Ke Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software supply-chain (SSC) attacks are increasingly multi-stage, cross-source, and temporally distributed. A single attack campaign may leave weak and fragmented traces across multi-source telemetry that captures different granularities and perspectives of runtime behavior. Existing runtime detection systems often analyze these sources independently, making it difficult to identify low-frequency attack evidence or reconstruct the temporal context in which it appears. We present FUSECHAIN, a runtime detection framework that represents multi-source software supply-chain telemetry as a temporal heterogeneous provenance graph over a unified event-time axis. By aligning package/runtime traces, process events, network telemetry, DNS/HTTP metadata, and security alerts on a unified temporal graph, FuseChain captures cross-source dependencies and sparse attack evidence that may be ambiguous within any individual source. It learns anomaly-centric temporal representations from benign-prefix telemetry and performs deployable attack-stage reconstruction through a lightweight decoder on top of a frozen anomaly backbone. Our experiments show that jointly optimizing anomaly detection and stage prediction is ineffective under sparse and imbalanced runtime supply-chain telemetry. Across seven SSC attack scenarios, FuseChain improves deployable stage reconstruction from 0.369 to 0.881 Stage Recall@500 with a frozen-backbone decoder, while adaptive retrieval further increases observable-stage recall from 0.524 to 0.655 without modifying the detector. These results highlight the deployable value of decoupling runtime SSC anomaly detection from downstream attack-stage interpretation.
tldr: FuseChain is a runtime detection framework for software supply-chain attacks that reconstructs attack stages from multi-source telemetry using temporal heterogeneous provenance graphs.
motivation: Existing runtime detection systems analyze telemetry sources independently, making it difficult to identify low-frequency attack evidence or reconstruct temporal context across multi-stage, cross-source attacks.
method: FuseChain aligns package/runtime traces, process events, network telemetry, DNS/HTTP metadata, and security alerts on a unified temporal graph, learns anomaly-centric representations from benign-prefix telemetry, and uses a lightweight decoder on a frozen anomaly backbone for attack-stage reconstruction.
result: Across seven SSC attack scenarios, FuseChain improves deployable stage reconstruction from 0.369 to 0.881 Stage Recall@500 with a frozen-backbone decoder, and adaptive retrieval increases observable-stage recall from 0.524 to 0.655.
conclusion: Decoupling runtime SSC anomaly detection from downstream attack-stage interpretation is effective for deployable attack reconstruction under sparse and imbalanced telemetry.

title: SkillVetBench: LLM-as-Judge For Multi-Dimensional Security Risk Evaluation In Open-Source Llm Agent Skills
authors: Ismail Hossain, Sai Puppala, Md Jahangir Alam, Tanzim Ahad, Sajedul Talukder
abstract: ArXiv:2606.15899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-source LLM agent ecosystems are growing rapidly, yet the security of community-contributed skills - modular tool definitions that extend agent capabilities - remains largely unvetted. The gap we fill: existing scanners operate at the code layer and are structurally blind to instruction-layer and multi-agent risk - natural-language directives that hijack an agent, exfiltrate data through encoded side channels, or chain harm across pipelines - so what is needed is a semantic, multi-dimensional vetting system rather than another signature matcher. We present SKILLVETBENCH, a live public leaderboard on Hugging Face that uses an LLM-as-Judge to vet agent skills. What is new: SARS (Skill Agentic Risk Score), a five-dimensional agentic-risk metric with a principled weighted formula for instruction-following systems. What is integrated: full CVSS v4.0 vector decomposition and a ClawHub dual-view that places our LLM-generated review beside the official marketplace verdict. What is demonstrated: drawing on our companion benchmark paper [ 1], the LLM-as-Judge stage achieves zero false negatives across 78 confirmed-malicious skills and zero false positives across 22 benign controls, while the best static baseline (SKILLSIEVE) still misses 15%; for instruction-layer categories such as Prompt Injection and Memory Poisoning, conventional tools miss between 89% and 100% of threats (e.g., CODEBERT detects none of nine memory-poisoning skills). Detection rates vary from 35% to 95% across four LLM evaluators, motivating ensemble scoring in production deployments.
tldr: This paper presents a benchmark and LLM-based evaluation framework for detecting security risks in open-source LLM agent skills, focusing on instruction-layer and multi-agent threats.
motivation: Existing code-level scanners fail to detect natural-language-based security risks in LLM agent skills, necessitating a semantic, multi-dimensional vetting system.
method: The authors propose SKILLVETBENCH, a live leaderboard using an LLM-as-Judge to evaluate agent skills across five risk dimensions, integrating CVSS v4.0 and a dual-view review system.
result: The LLM-as-Judge achieves zero false negatives on 78 malicious skills and zero false positives on 22 benign controls, outperforming static baselines that miss up to 100% of instruction-layer threats.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates high effectiveness for security vetting of LLM agent skills, but the paper is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stickel-type Key Exchange With Hidden Subspaces
authors: Paul Watts Fintan Costello
abstract: ArXiv:2606.16021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a witness-finding cryptanalysis of Stickel-type key exchange schemes, which involve two-sided multiplication of [MATH] matrices over [MATH], where these matrices are drawn from public subspaces with a particular commuting structure. This analysis covers Stickel's original proposal , Shpilrain's polynomial extension of that scheme, Nager's algebraic extension of that scheme, and more generally all Stickel-type approaches using public subspaces over matrix algebra in finite fields: all such schemes can be broken in polynomial time. We also describe a new key establishment scheme using two-sided matrix multiplication in which the commuting subspaces used to form the key are hidden via conjugation by private terms, blocking this specific public-subspace analysis; the witness-finding problem in this new scheme has a direct reduction from a standard NP-hard problem (Edmonds' problem).
tldr: This paper presents a cryptanalysis of Stickel-type key exchange schemes and proposes a new scheme based on hidden subspaces, with a reduction from Edmonds' problem.
motivation: Stickel-type key exchange schemes are vulnerable to polynomial-time attacks; the authors aim to develop a more secure variant.
method: The authors provide a witness-finding cryptanalysis using public subspace structure, then design a new scheme where commuting subspaces are hidden via conjugation, reducing security to a standard NP-hard problem.
result: All Stickel-type schemes with public subspaces are broken in polynomial time; the new hidden-subspace scheme resists this attack and is NP-hard to break.
conclusion: The new scheme offers a provably secure alternative to Stickel-type key exchange, though practical implementation details are not addressed.

title: The Anatomy Of Scam Scenarios: Large-Scale Characterization And Conversation-Aware Detection
authors: Shang Ma, Chen Yanai, Avichai Ben, Zichen Liu, Yanfang Ye, Xusheng Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.16052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online scams have become a pervasive global threat, causing substantial financial, psychological, and operational harm. Scammers embed psychological techniques (PTs) within reusable operational schemes to scale scam campaigns with minimal adaptation. However, existing studies often analyze PTs as isolated features, overlooking the recurring scam scenarios in which they are systematically deployed. To address this gap, we first conduct a large-scale empirical study to jointly characterize scam scenarios and their associated PTs. Specifically, we develop a data-driven pipeline to derive a hierarchical taxonomy of scam scenarios, consisting of 18 fine-grained scenarios grouped into 6 high-level tactics based on their PT profiles. Furthermore, to transfer this scenario-level knowledge to practical defense, we design a conversation-aware scam scenario detection approach for financial-institution customer interactions, enabling timely warning and intervention. Our study on 102,054 real-world scam incident reports, spanning 2024-02-01 to 2025-10-31, reveals that PT usage is significantly associated with scam scenarios. We further show that scammers organize scenarios around different operational goals, such as broad victim exposure, high victim conversion, and high-value extraction, and reuse infrastructure, including IP addresses, domains, email addresses, and phone numbers, to launch coordinated campaigns at scale. Evaluation on.
tldr: This paper studies online scam scenarios and proposes a conversation-aware detection method using a large dataset of scam incident reports.
motivation: Existing studies analyze psychological techniques in scams as isolated features, overlooking the recurring scam scenarios in which they are systematically deployed.
method: The authors develop a data-driven pipeline to derive a hierarchical taxonomy of scam scenarios and design a conversation-aware scam scenario detection approach for financial-institution customer interactions.
result: Analysis of 102,054 real-world scam incident reports reveals that psychological technique usage is significantly associated with scam scenarios, and scammers reuse infrastructure for coordinated campaigns.
conclusion: The proposed detection approach can enable timely warning and intervention in financial-institution customer interactions.

motivation: To address the challenge of developing p-type transparent oxide semiconductors with ultrawide band gaps for optoelectronic applications.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to analyze electronic structure and defect properties.
result: The material is intrinsically n-type, not p-type as previously reported, due to oxygen vacancies and other donor defects.
conclusion: Spinel LiGa5O8 is not a viable p-type ultrawide band gap semiconductor; alternative materials or doping strategies are needed.

title: Amplitude Variation In Spanwise Wall Oscillations: Effects On Drag Reduction And Heat Transfer In Compressible Turbulent Channel Flow
authors: Fangliang Xu, Wei Liu, And Peng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Fangliang Xu, Wei Liu, and Peng Zhang

Spanwise Wall Oscillation is a promising active flow control technique for turbulent skin-friction drag reduction (DR). While the effectiveness of the method in incompressible flows is well documented, its performance in compressible regimes, and the underlying physical mechanisms, particularly thos…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065105] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies drag reduction and heat transfer in compressible turbulent channel flow using spanwise wall oscillations, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the effectiveness of spanwise wall oscillation for drag reduction in compressible flows, which is less explored than in incompressible flows.
method: Numerical simulations of compressible turbulent channel flow with spanwise wall oscillations, analyzing amplitude variation effects on drag and heat transfer.
result: The study quantifies how amplitude variation affects drag reduction and heat transfer in compressible turbulent flow.
conclusion: Spanwise wall oscillation can be effective for drag reduction in compressible flows, but the effects on heat transfer must be considered.

title: Kinetic And Fluid Descriptions Of Jeans Instability In Kappa-distributed Suprathermal Astrophysical Plasmas
authors: Pooja Dalal And Ram Prasad Prajapati
abstract:
Author(s): Pooja Dalal and Ram Prasad Prajapati

The Jeans instability in an unmagnetized, collisionless self-gravitating plasma characterized by a kappa or Lorentzian velocity distribution is investigated in the framework of kinetic and fluid approaches. We have examined the role of suprathermality on the instability threshold wave number and gro…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065208] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Jeans instability in suprathermal astrophysical plasmas using kinetic and fluid models, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the effect of suprathermal (kappa-distributed) particles on the gravitational collapse threshold in astrophysical plasmas.
method: Kinetic theory with kappa distribution and fluid equations are used to derive dispersion relations and instability criteria.
result: Suprathermality modifies the Jeans wavenumber and growth rate compared to Maxwellian plasmas.
conclusion: The kappa distribution significantly affects the Jeans instability, which is important for astrophysical structure formation.

title: Wake-tail Effects In Two-dimensional Wave Refocusing
authors: Theodoros T. Koutserimpas
abstract:
Author(s): Theodoros T. Koutserimpas

In even spatial dimensions, solutions of the wave equation violate Huygens' principle, producing a persistent wake tail inside the light cone rather than a sharply localized propagating front. This intrinsic tail complicates refocusing. Here, we examine how the wake-tail structure of the two-dimensi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065102] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wake-tail effects in two-dimensional wave refocusing, a topic in classical wave physics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding how the violation of Huygens' principle in even dimensions affects wave refocusing is a fundamental problem in classical wave theory.
method: The author analytically and numerically examines the wake-tail structure of the two-dimensional wave equation and its impact on refocusing.
result: The wake tail causes persistent disturbances that complicate refocusing, with specific quantitative effects characterized.
conclusion: The wake-tail effect is an intrinsic feature of two-dimensional wave propagation that must be accounted for in refocusing applications.

title: Resonance Behavior Of A Bubble Near A Spherical Inclusion
authors: Thomas Micol, Alexander A. Doinikov, Cyril Mauger, And Claude Inserra
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Micol, Alexander A. Doinikov, Cyril Mauger, and Claude Inserra

We present an analytical model for the frequency response of a gas microbubble oscillating near a spherical inclusion of arbitrary size and mechanical nature (rigid, fluid, or viscoelastic) immersed in a viscous compressible fluid. The model considers both radial and nonspherical oscillations in the…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065103] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the resonance behavior of a gas microbubble near a spherical inclusion in a viscous fluid, with applications in medical ultrasound and cavitation.
motivation: Understanding bubble dynamics near inclusions is important for applications like targeted drug delivery and ultrasound imaging, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: An analytical model is developed for the frequency response of a bubble oscillating near a spherical inclusion, considering radial and nonspherical modes and various inclusion properties.
result: The model predicts resonance frequencies and damping effects depending on inclusion size and mechanical properties.
conclusion: The work provides insights into bubble-inclusion interactions but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Humidity As A Critical Parameter For Predicting Breakdown Voltage In Submicrometer Electrode Gaps In Air
authors: B. Disson, N. Bonifaci, O. Lesaint, C. Poulain, R. Dussart, And S. Iseni
abstract:
Author(s): B. Disson, N. Bonifaci, O. Lesaint, C. Poulain, R. Dussart, and S. Iseni

This experimental work reinvestigates the breakdown voltage in air for electrode gaps ranging from [MATH] to [MATH]. Rarely addressed in the literature of the field, a special focus is placed on varying the gas humidity and its direct impact on the breakdown vo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065207] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies the effect of humidity on breakdown voltage in submicrometer electrode gaps in air.
motivation: Understanding breakdown voltage in small gaps is important for microelectronics and insulation design, but humidity effects are rarely addressed.
method: Experimental measurements of breakdown voltage in air for electrode gaps from 0.5 to 10 μm under controlled humidity conditions.
result: Humidity significantly affects breakdown voltage, with higher humidity reducing the breakdown voltage.
conclusion: Humidity must be considered as a critical parameter for predicting breakdown in submicrometer gaps.

title: Linear Rayleigh-Taylor Instability With Foams
authors: A. Bret, A. J. Devault, S. G. Dannhoff, M. Gatu Johnson, C. K. Li, And J. A. Frenje
abstract:
Author(s): A. Bret, A. J. DeVault, S. G. Dannhoff, M. Gatu Johnson, C. K. Li, and J. A. Frenje

We analyze the behavior of the linear phase of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI) in the presence of a foam. Such a problem may be relevant, for example, to some inertial confinement fusion (ICF) scenarios such as foams within the capsule or lining the inner hohlraum wall. The foam displays three…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065409] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the linear phase of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability in the presence of foam, relevant to inertial confinement fusion.
motivation: Understanding the effect of foam on Rayleigh-Taylor instability is important for improving inertial confinement fusion designs.
method: The authors perform a linear stability analysis of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability with a foam modeled as a porous medium.
result: They find that the foam can reduce the growth rate of the instability under certain conditions.
conclusion: Foam liners may help mitigate Rayleigh-Taylor instability in inertial confinement fusion capsules.

title: Feasibility And Single Parameter Scaling Of Extinctions In Large Ecological Communities
authors: Philippe Jacquod
abstract:
Author(s): Philippe Jacquod

Multispecies ecosystems modeled by generalized Lotka-Volterra equations exhibit stationary population abundances, where a large number of species often coexist. Understanding the precise conditions under which this is at all feasible and what triggers species extinctions is a key, outstanding proble…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062202] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies species extinctions in large ecological communities using generalized Lotka-Volterra equations.
motivation: Understanding the conditions for species coexistence and extinction triggers is a key problem in ecology.
method: The authors analyze stationary population abundances in multispecies ecosystems modeled by generalized Lotka-Volterra equations.
result: They identify a single parameter scaling that governs extinctions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the feasibility of coexistence and extinction dynamics in large ecological communities.

title: Higher-order Contagion Processes In 3.99 Dimensions
authors: Sandro Meloni, Andrea Gabrielli, And Pablo Villegas
abstract:
Author(s): Sandro Meloni, Andrea Gabrielli, and Pablo Villegas

Higher-order interactions have recently emerged as a promising framework for describing new dynamical phenomena in heterogeneous contagion processes. However, a fundamental open question is how to understand their contribution from the perspective of the physics of critical phenomena. Based on a mes…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order contagion processes from a critical phenomena perspective in 3.99 dimensions.
motivation: Understanding the role of higher-order interactions in contagion dynamics is an open question, especially from the viewpoint of critical phenomena.
method: The authors use a mesoscopic approach and renormalization group techniques to analyze contagion models with higher-order interactions near the upper critical dimension.
result: They derive scaling laws and critical exponents for the contagion process in 3.99 dimensions.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions modify the critical behavior of contagion processes, but the paper is purely in the domain of statistical physics and network science, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Innate Behavioral Mechanisms And Defensive Traits In Ecological Models Of Predator-prey Types
authors: Sangeeta Saha, Swadesh Pal, And Roderick Melnik
abstract:
Author(s): Sangeeta Saha, Swadesh Pal, and Roderick Melnik

Phenotypic plasticity enables prey species to develop inducible defences in response to predation risk, significantly influencing predator-prey interactions. In this study, we propose a nonlinear predator-prey model in which prey exhibit inducible defense mechanisms, while predators experience mutua…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064203] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper models predator-prey dynamics with inducible prey defenses and mutual interference among predators using nonlinear differential equations.
motivation: To understand how phenotypic plasticity in prey and mutual interference among predators affect ecological stability and population dynamics.
method: A nonlinear predator-prey model is proposed and analyzed using dynamical systems theory, including stability analysis and bifurcation analysis.
result: The model exhibits complex dynamics such as limit cycles and bistability, showing that inducible defenses and mutual interference can stabilize or destabilize the system depending on parameters.
conclusion: Inducible defenses and predator mutual interference are key factors in shaping predator-prey interactions and should be considered in ecological management.

title: Zonal Magnetic Fields Regulate Nonlinear Edge-localized-mode Dynamics Via Self-consistent Force Balance
authors: Nami Li, Xueqiao Xu, Ben Dudson, Rob Falgout, And Giorgis Georgakoudis
abstract:
Author(s): Nami Li, Xueqiao Xu, Ben Dudson, Rob Falgout, and Giorgis Georgakoudis

Edge-localized modes (ELMs) eject intense bursts of heat and particles that threaten plasma-facing components in fusion reactors. Nonlinear full-torus [MATH] simulations show that turbulence-driven zonal magnetic fields (ZMFs) play an essential role in nonlinear ELM evolution by maintaini…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065204] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies zonal magnetic fields in fusion plasma edge-localized modes, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: Edge-localized modes threaten fusion reactor components; understanding their nonlinear dynamics is crucial for reactor design.
method: Full-torus nonlinear MHD simulations are used to model ELM evolution and the role of zonal magnetic fields.
result: Turbulence-driven zonal magnetic fields regulate ELM dynamics through self-consistent force balance.
conclusion: Zonal magnetic fields are essential for controlling ELM bursts in fusion plasmas.

title: Effects Of Hydrodynamic Motion On The Stopping Power And Energy Deposition Of Alpha Particles In An Inertial Confinement Fusion Hotspot
authors: Bao Du, Dongguo Kang, Peilin Yao, Fengjun Ge, Zhensheng Dai, Shiyang Zou, Zongqiang Yuan, Lianqiang Shan, Hongbo Cai, And Shaoping Zhu
abstract:

The outflow velocity of expanding deuterium-tritium (DT) fuel can become significant after the bangtime, approaching local ion thermal velocity when the inertial confinement fusion (ICF) hotspot surpasses the ignition threshold. Under such conditions, the conventional assumption of an isotropic targ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065206] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of hydrodynamic motion on alpha particle stopping power in inertial confinement fusion hotspots.
motivation: In ICF, after ignition, the DT fuel expands with velocities comparable to thermal velocities, invalidating the usual isotropic target assumption. Accurate energy deposition modeling is needed for ignition and burn.
method: The authors derive a modified stopping power formula accounting for hydrodynamic motion and perform numerical simulations of alpha particle transport in a dynamic hotspot.
result: Hydrodynamic motion reduces the stopping power and energy deposition of alpha particles, leading to a longer range and altered heating profile.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic effects must be included in ICF burn simulations for accurate predictions of ignition and yield.

title: Controlled Interference Of Laser-induced Shock Waves In Microdroplet Jetting
authors: R. A. Meijer, G. Lajoinie, B. Liu, S. Witte, And O. O. Versolato

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023287] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies laser-induced shock wave interference to produce high-velocity microjets from tin microdroplets, with applications in extreme ultraviolet lithography.
motivation: To understand and control the formation of microjets for industrial applications such as EUV light sources.
method: Experimental: two laser pulses create interfering shock waves in a tin droplet, and high-speed imaging captures the resulting jet dynamics.
result: The interference pattern can be tuned to control jet velocity and direction, achieving high-speed jets.
conclusion: Controlled interference of shock waves enables precise microjetting, relevant for lithography but not for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Circular Dichroism In The Photoelectron Angular Distribution Of Achiral Molecules
authors: Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto de Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, And Peter Puschnig

Circular dichroism in the angular distribution (CDAD) is the effect that the angular intensity distribution of photoemitted electrons depends on the handedness of the incident circularly polarized light. The origin of CDAD can be manifold, including intrinsic properties of the system under study, su…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023275] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distributions from achiral molecules, focusing on the role of molecular orientation and final-state scattering.
motivation: Understanding the origin of circular dichroism in photoemission from achiral molecules is important for interpreting experimental data and for potential applications in molecular imaging.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements of photoelectron angular distributions with theoretical simulations using multiple scattering and density functional theory.
result: They show that circular dichroism arises from the interplay between molecular orientation and final-state scattering effects, even in the absence of molecular chirality.
conclusion: The findings clarify the mechanisms behind CDAD in achiral systems and provide a framework for analyzing such effects in more complex molecules.

title: Sea-surface Retention Effect Shapes Ocean Microplastic Fibers
authors: Andrea Mazzino And Giuseppe Suaria
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Mazzino and Giuseppe Suaria

Microfibers contaminate the global ocean, but their impact depends on length-dependent residence at the air-sea interface. In the submillimeter range, the sea surface exhibits a surface-enrichment signature: The long-to-short fiber ratio is higher at the interface than a few meters below (about 5 m)…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023283] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the length-dependent retention of microplastic fibers at the ocean surface, finding that longer fibers are enriched at the air-sea interface compared to subsurface waters.
motivation: Microplastic fibers are a major pollutant in the ocean, but their vertical distribution and residence time at the surface are poorly understood, which affects their environmental impact.
method: The authors combine field measurements of fiber length distributions at the sea surface and at 5 m depth with a theoretical model of turbulent mixing and buoyancy to explain the observed enrichment.
result: They find a significant surface enrichment of long fibers (length > 0.5 mm) relative to short fibers, consistent with a balance between turbulent diffusion and buoyant rise.
conclusion: The sea surface acts as a selective retention layer for longer microplastic fibers, which has implications for their transport, degradation, and ingestion by marine organisms.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Dephasing Reduction In An Optically Guided Laser-plasma Accelerator
authors: Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, And Cédric Thaury
abstract:

Laser-plasma accelerators offer a compact means of producing high-energy electron beams, but their performance is fundamentally limited by dephasing between the accelerated electrons and the plasma wave. To overcome this limitation, we investigate the combination of plasma density tapering and optic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023274] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates dephasing reduction in a laser-plasma accelerator using plasma density tapering and optical guiding.
motivation: Laser-plasma accelerators are limited by dephasing between electrons and the plasma wave; overcoming this is crucial for improving electron beam energy and quality.
method: The authors experimentally combine plasma density tapering with optical guiding to extend the acceleration length and reduce dephasing.
result: They observe a significant reduction in dephasing, leading to higher-energy electron beams compared to standard configurations.
conclusion: The technique offers a practical path to enhance the performance of laser-plasma accelerators for compact high-energy applications.

title: Generation Of Attosecond Pulses From Relativistic Oscillating Plasma Gratings
authors: Hao-Jie Zhang, Bo-Yuan Li, Xiang-Yan An, Rong Huang, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Feng Liu, And Min Chen

We propose a scheme to generate two isolated attosecond pulses at controllable angles through the interaction between relativistic laser pulses and a solid target. tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate attosecond pulses using relativistic oscillating plasma gratings driven by chirped laser pulses.
motivation: Attosecond pulse generation is important for ultrafast science, and the authors aim to produce isolated attosecond pulses at controllable angles.
method: Two chirped, p-polarized relativistic laser pulses interact with a solid target to create oscillating plasma gratings, which reflect the pulses to generate attosecond pulses.
result: The scheme yields two isolated attosecond pulses with controllable emission angles and durations.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a new way to generate attosecond pulses with angular control, potentially useful for pump-probe experiments.

title: Unified Model For Full-stage Shear Thickening Via Surface Chemistry And Friction

tldr: This paper proposes a constitutive model for shear thickening fluids based on surface chemistry and friction, unifying three rheological stages.
motivation: Shear thickening fluids exhibit complex state transitions under varying conditions, and understanding the molecular-level mechanisms is important for applications.
method: The authors develop a constitutive model that incorporates surface chemistry and friction effects to describe shear thinning, shear thickening, and the transition between them.
result: The model successfully unifies the three rheological stages and matches experimental data.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for shear thickening behavior, with potential implications for material design.

title: Inhibitory Synaptic Timescales Drive Oscillatory Regime Transitions In Recurrent Excitatory-inhibitory Networks
authors: Siamak Kheiri, Saeed Taghavi, Matjaž Perc, And Alireza Valizadeh

In recurrent cortical networks, inhibitory kinetics are often assumed to tune oscillation frequency continuously. Using a recurrent excitatory-inhibitory (E-I) model with fixed excitatory synaptic dynamics, we systematically vary inhibitory decay time constants and show instead that inhibitory times…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023251] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how inhibitory synaptic timescales drive transitions between oscillatory regimes in a recurrent excitatory-inhibitory network model.
motivation: To understand how inhibitory kinetics shape network oscillations in cortical circuits.
method: Systematic variation of inhibitory decay time constants in a recurrent E-I model with fixed excitatory dynamics.
result: Inhibitory timescales cause discrete regime transitions rather than continuous frequency tuning.
conclusion: Inhibitory kinetics play a critical role in determining oscillatory dynamics, with implications for neural computation.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.

motivation: Resonant modes typically have narrow bandwidths, limiting their application in broadband flow stabilization.
method: The authors propose a super-resonance mechanism that maintains a broadband out-of-phase response beyond conventional resonance bandwidth.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications.
conclusion: The concept of super-resonance breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, offering new possibilities for flow control.

result: The theory provides a new design principle for Hookean metashells.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and connect these observations to bulk hydrogel behavior via a force-response model.
result: They identify key molecular determinants of fatigue and demonstrate how protein unfolding/refolding cycles govern macroscopic fracture.
conclusion: The work provides a design strategy for fatigue-resistant hydrogels based on molecular-level insights.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change

method: The authors use a vapor training process to induce mesopore changes in wood-derived nanocrystal films and characterize the resulting mechanical properties.
result: The vapor training process improves plasticity and enables better shaping of the films.
conclusion: The study demonstrates a method to enhance plasticity in nanocrystal films through mesopore engineering, relevant for materials engineering but not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets

result: Cells at topological defects experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng

method: Experimental three-dimensional flow measurements around a free-swimming alga.
result: Discovery of unexpected flow structures at low Reynolds numbers.

title: Active Hydrodynamic Theory Of Euchromatin And Heterochromatin
authors: S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, And Michael J. Shelley
abstract:

Researchers develop a theoretical framework that shows how mechanical forces and flows drive the spatial segregation and nucleus-wide patterning of chromatin in cells.
